texts: Indonesian President Joko Widodo has confirmed that the executions of drug smugglers Andrew Chan and Myuran Sukumaran are imminent, as soon as all legal appeals have been concluded. The pair, along with eight other death row prisoners, are currently awaiting the results of their appeals. President Widodo stated that the executions would take place upon the conclusion of all legal procedures, and that it was only a matter of time before they were carried out. Chan and Sukumaran are currently in an isolated cell on Nusakambangan Island, where they have lodged a challenge with the Constitutional Court to have their death sentence overturned. The executions have been delayed until after the Asian African conference being held in Jakarta this week.

A heartfelt letter written by a passenger to a pilot thanking them for safely bringing her home has gone viral on Twitter, just a week after the Germanwings tragedy. The letter, written by a passenger known as 'Bethanie', expresses her gratitude to the pilot and airline for allowing her to live in Spain while splitting her time with family in England. The letter has been shared over 3,700 times and has been favourited almost 3,000 times, with many praising the role of the pilot. The letter was posted by pilot Jai Dillon, who was unable to reveal the airline or flight number due to security reasons. Investigations are continuing into the Germanwings crash, where pilot Andreas Lubitz is believed to have deliberately caused the crash. The letter has created a ripple effect of compassion and understanding among those in the industry.

Japan's Defense Minister, Gen Nakatani, assured lawmakers that Japan has never been invaded by aliens and no government studies into extra-terrestrials are underway. The assurance came after an inquiry from an MP, Antonio Inoki, who had asked if aircraft were dispatched to meet extra-terrestrial visitors and if studies on aliens were ongoing. Inoki had once seen a mysterious flying object, but Nakatani said that no unidentified flying objects believed to have come from anywhere other than Earth had been found. In 2007, the Japanese government had issued a statement saying they had not confirmed the existence of unidentified flying objects believed to have come from anywhere other than Earth, but the statement was later retracted by the top government spokesman who believed in the existence of UFOs controlled by alien life-forms.

Nearly half of headteachers in the UK are struggling to fill vacancies in core subjects such as English, maths and science due to a worsening recruitment crisis in secondary schools. The situation is expected to get worse due to increasing pupil numbers and greater competition for graduates among employers. The survey by the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) found that 44% of respondents had vacancies in English, 52% in maths and 50% in science. London schools are experiencing the most difficulties in recruiting teachers for these subjects, followed by the North West and East of England. Non-core subjects such as geography, design and technology, business studies, computer science, religious education and modern foreign languages are also facing recruitment difficulties. The survey received 97 responses from headteachers and groups of headteachers from local networks of schools. One headteacher in southern England said they had only one applicant for a head of maths position, while a headteacher in the East of England said they had two suitable candidates out of four applicants for a head of ICT/computing position. The union is proposing a ten-point plan to deal with the recruitment crisis, including an expansion in school-led teacher training, the development of a core curriculum for teaching degrees and the launch of a campaign to attract new recruits.

An Indian salesman in the United Arab Emirates is facing up to seven years in prison and a fine of up to £186,000 for allegedly cursing Islam and the Prophet Mohammad on Facebook. The man, identified as S.G., is accused of posting a blasphemous status after watching a news bulletin about the war in Iraq. He initially claimed he received the image over Whatsapp, but later admitted to posting the status. If found guilty, he could face imprisonment and a large fine. The UAE considers blasphemy a serious criminal offense and regularly censors materials critical of Islam. The salesman failed to attend a court hearing on Monday and the case was adjourned until April 27. In 2011, a British tourist was also taken to court in Dubai for calling the Islamic prophet a 'terrorist'.

A father from Coventry, Marcin Wasniewski, escaped death by a mere millimeter when his car collided with the back of a lorry on the A444. Emergency services were shocked to find him alive and unharmed, as the car had embedded itself into the back of the lorry. Marcin suffered injuries to his face and arm but is now volunteering at a Christian center until he can return to work. He believes his survival was a result of divine intervention. Paramedics were amazed that he had escaped life-threatening injuries, as the impact would have been fatal if it had been just a few inches closer to the driver or if there had been a passenger in the car. Marcin is currently unable to work due to his injuries but is recovering. He also spoke of how he remembers the accident but then blacked out and woke up in the hospital. The crash caused significant damage to the car and trailer.

A European eagle owl has been terrorizing the Dutch town of Noordeinde for months, launching itself from rooftops onto unsuspecting birdwatchers' heads. The bird, which is believed to have escaped from an aviary, has been associated with food by humans and has been drawing twitchers from around the country. The owl, which has a wingspan of up to 75cm and weighs around 6lbs, spends an average of one minute perched on the head of its victims before flying off. The European eagle owl is one of the largest species of owls and is found in a variety of habitats. The rogue owl has been causing vicious attacks and has been drawing twitchers to the town in hopes of catching a sighting. Menno Scheefer, a photographer from Zaandam, Netherlands, travelled 68km to the town to photograph the owl. The owl has been causing confusion and terror in the town for months.

A 100-year-old man from New Jersey, Michael Juskin, is accused of killing his 88-year-old wife Rosalia with an ax while she slept and then committing suicide with a knife. The couple had a history of domestic issues, but a motive for the murder-suicide has not been determined. Neighbors were visibly upset after discovering the bodies on Monday morning. Michael Juskin is one of the oldest people ever to be accused of homicide. The couple had mental health issues and had been the subject of police visits in recent years. Michael had been suffering from dementia and his wife had wanted to move to Florida, but he wanted to keep their New Jersey home. Police have not yet determined a motive for the killings.

Sherrell Dillion, a single mother from Benefits Street, has landed a place in the Top Model of Colour competition despite being currently homeless. She has been striving for a career in modelling for years and hopes this will be her big break. She wishes her former neighbour White Dee all the success in the world and hopes to use the show to better herself. Sherrell became homeless after her house was infested with mice and is now living in temporary accommodation in Handsworth. She was scouted at the age of 22 but then suffered an ectopic pregnancy that left her bedridden for months. The final of Top Model of Colour UK takes place on May 30 and the winner will receive a modelling contract, jewellery, clothes and shoes as well as other prizes.

A border guard was killed in a cross-border fire exchange with militants in Yemen this week, marking Saudi Arabia's first publicly known military death since it launched airstrikes against rebels inside its southern neighbor. Houthi rebels seized the presidential palace in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden, and Yemeni special forces loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh arrived in an attempt to secure the city. U.S. Navy warships were patrolling off Yemen in search of suspicious shipping in the region, and a Panamanian-registered cargo ship was found to be carrying cement and construction materials. Marie Claire Feghali described events in Aden as "extremely fluid and very, very complicated," and a hospital near heavy fighting was forced to shut down. Additionally, Al Qaeda fighters were reported to have freed 270 prisoners from Yemeni prisons.

Royal Bank of Scotland (RBS) reported a loss of £446 million for the first three months of the year, bringing its total losses since the 2008 bailout to £50 billion. The loss includes provisions for fines, lawsuits, and compensation for mis-sold financial products. RBS also reported a £453 million restructuring charge due to a slump in the value of premises in the US. The loss is a blow to taxpayers, who own 80% of the bank, and comes at an awkward time for Chancellor George Osborne, six days before the General Election. RBS was hit with fines in the US and the UK, and former CEO Fred Goodwin was knighted and later stripped of his title. RBS CEO Ross McEwan warned of more conduct and litigation hurdles ahead. The losses wiped more than £700 million off the value of RBS shares, and the TaxPayers' Alliance criticized the last Labour government for failing to regulate the banks.

Kenny Bayless, a veteran referee from Las Vegas, has been appointed to oversee the highly anticipated Mayweather vs. Pacquiao fight on May 2. Both camps are pleased with the decision, as Bayless has refereed previous fights involving Mayweather and Pacquiao. The Nevada State Athletic Commission has put their trust in Bayless's large physical presence and unflappable personality, as the fight is expected to attract a large audience. Bayless will receive $25,000 for the night's work, while the judges will each receive $20,000. Serious consideration was given to including a judge from overseas, but Glenn Feldman from Connecticut was ultimately chosen. Bayless has refereed previous super fights involving Mayweather and Pacquiao, and will receive more than expected for his services. The fight is expected to go the 12-round distance, and both fighters are expected to earn minimums of $180 million and $120 million, respectively. Pacquiao and Mayweather continue their training ahead of the super-fight.

A hospital in Henan Province, China, is being moved eight meters a day on 1,000 metal rollers to avoid demolition for a new road. The two-storey brick building, which is 1,700 square meters in size, requires more than 1,000 wheels to move. Engineers aim to move the building 17.5 meters to its new spot. The project is expected to be completed in a few days and is not the first time engineers in China have moved a building in this way. In 2013, a six-storey building in Shanghai was moved 38 meters and in 2004, the Fu gang Building in Guangxi Province was moved 36 meters and took 11 days to complete. The building is placed on metal plates with cylinder-shaped rollers wedged between them.

Real Madrid's teen sensation Martin Odegaard was starstruck when he met former Brazil international Ronaldo at the club's training ground. Odegaard, who joined Real Madrid in January, has been training with the first team regularly and was in awe of the former World Cup winning striker. Ronaldo, who scored over 100 goals for Real and netted 62 international goals, was visiting his old club ahead of their Champions League quarter-final second-leg clash against Atletico Madrid. Odegaard has found life tough at the Spanish giants in recent weeks after being dropped from the Castilla side by first team coach Zinedine Zidane. Real Madrid are desperate for the Castilla side to win promotion to the second tier of Spanish football and Zidane must decide whether Odegaard's presence in the side is hindering their chances.

A woman named Margaret Hesketh, 70, died in a hospital in Wigan, England in October 2014. Her family claims that doctors wrongly diagnosed her with terminal cancer and put her on a Liverpool Care Pathway-style treatment for the dying, which involved removing her fluid and nutrition drips. However, a post-mortem found no evidence of cancer and she died of pneumonia while malnourished. The family is calling for a criminal investigation and the hospital has confirmed that they no longer use the Liverpool Care Pathway. The inquest is scheduled for this week. The woman's daughter, Karen Masters, is demanding answers and wants to know why her mother died in this way. The hospital has stated that they cannot give any more details due to patient confidentiality, but more information will be revealed at the public inquest. The hospital also confirmed that they stopped using the Liverpool Care Pathway in July 2014. The woman was admitted to the hospital with an infected bed sore and suspected pneumonia and doctors ruled out surgery due to her poor general health. She was a smoker who suffered from lung disease and had a heart attack 12 years ago. The family was told that a scan had revealed cancer and that she probably had less than three months to live. The family noticed that her feeding tubes had been removed and asked for them to be put back, but were told it would cause unnecessary distress. She died six days later. The hospital has stated that they will give a more balanced view of events at the public inquest. The Liverpool Care Pathway was a controversial end-of-life care plan that was phased out in 2013 after a review uncovered cases of patients suffering from dehydration before their deaths. Barcelona won against Celta Vigo in La Liga, with Neymar, Dani Alves and Adriano all playing key roles. The trio were seen wearing matching denim outfits in a post-match photo on social media. Mathieu, who scored the winning goal, admitted his side struggled due to the international break. Pique was praised for his defensive performance. The win saw Barcelona return to the top of the La Liga table.

Aydian Ethan Dowling, a transgender man from Oregon, is leading the Men's Health Magazine's Ultimate Guy Search with around 40,000 votes, 30,000 more than his closest competitor. He is widely touted to be the cover star of the magazine, which aims to find a man who embodies the qualities of a well-rounded, active, health-conscious and thoughtful guy. Aydian, who transitioned in 2009, lives with his wife of three years Jenilee and is a role model for transgender, gay, bisexual, and heterosexual men. He has launched his own sportswear brand, Point5cc, and is confident of winning over the magazine's judging panel. If he wins, he would make history as the magazine's first transgender cover star. The public vote counts for only 10% of the vote, but Aydian is optimistic about his chances. He is an Iraq war veteran and amputee, who clinched the top spot last year. The magazine is looking for a guy who is physically fit, leads a healthy lifestyle, has overcome challenges in his life, and somebody who readers can learn something from. Aydian embodies these values and is a strong contender for the cover. He is also an entrepreneur and has a hit YouTube channel. He loves hiking and being outside and is determined to find peace within his soul. He is confident that he has what it takes to win over the judges and make history as the magazine's first transgender cover star.

Manchester Airport temporarily suspended flights after a drone was reported in the area, causing disruption for hundreds of travellers. All flights were halted for about 20 minutes and some were delayed or diverted while police searched for the drone. Flights resumed after the search failed to find any evidence of a drone. Unmanned drones have become a problem for airports and pilots due to their popularity and potential danger. The Civil Aviation Authority has successfully prosecuted two drone operators for safety breaches. Drones cannot be flown beyond the normal unaided line of sight of the operator, must always be flown at least 164ft away from a person, vehicle, building or structure, and must never be flown within 492ft of a congested area or large group of people. Police continue to investigate the report of the sighting.

YouTube is celebrating its 10th anniversary and has become a major platform for content creators. To improve the quality of content, YouTube has opened "YouTube Spaces" in different cities, providing resources and training for independent filmmakers and creators. These spaces have helped break down barriers for low budget productions and have attracted more subscribers in different markets. Japanese film and TV company Toei is partnering with YouTube to encourage more Japanese samurai dramas and attract new subscribers. The goal is to raise the bar for YouTube content and provide financial rewards for popular videos. Many popular YouTube creators earn six-figure incomes through ad revenue and sponsorships.

Sutherland Council in Sydney is considering allowing campervans to park at allocated beach locations to deter tourists from neglecting certain areas due to a lack of accommodation. This proposal was put forward by Councillor Steve Simpson due to the economic benefits that backpackers bring to the area. However, some locals have had a negative response to the idea, citing concerns about rising land values and the potential for disorderly behaviour. Mayor Kent Johns is keen to attract more tourists while keeping away those who act in an unwelcome manner. President of the Cronulla Chamber of Commerce, Mark Aprilovic, disagrees with the proposal and believes it cannot be done without offending local people. Some believe that rezoning open park areas may be necessary to make this feasible.

Jordan Henderson has signed a new five-year £100,000-a-week contract with Liverpool, committing his long-term future to the club. He had the opportunity to leave Liverpool in 2012 but decided to stay and prove himself. Henderson has enjoyed a strong campaign and could be handed the captain's armband when Steven Gerrard leaves. He is determined to help Liverpool win trophies and turn potential into success. Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers hopes other players, including Raheem Sterling, will follow Henderson's lead and sign new deals. Henderson arrived from Sunderland in 2011 and has been developed into an important player for the club. Liverpool is working hard to develop young players and keep them at the club for the best part of their careers.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, has pleaded guilty to attempting to buy the biological toxin abrin from undercover police on the dark web. The dark web is a subsection of the deep web and is used for sharing information and trading goods anonymously and encrypted. The teenager was caught after expressing an interest in acquiring the toxin and was aware of its toxicity and potential for harm. He will be sentenced later this month for the offence, which is contrary to the Criminal Attempts Act 1981 and Section 1 of the Biological Weapons Act 1974. The dark web has been used for illegal activities such as selling drugs and hacked information. Last year, a graphic designer was the first person to be prosecuted under the Biological Weapons Act for attempting to poison her mother using a substance obtained on the dark web.

Georgia Governor Nathan Deal signed a bill on Thursday that will legalize low-THC cannabis oil for certain medical conditions, such as epilepsy. This comes after a family, the Coxes, moved to Colorado to get the marijuana extract for their 5-year-old daughter, Haleigh, who was having hundreds of seizures a day and the five potent drugs meant to control them weren't helping. The bill, known as Haleigh's Hope Act, will create an infrastructure, registration process and research program for the drug. This will benefit not only people who suffer from chronic seizure disorders, but also allow patients to receive in-state treatment. The law is specific to a handful of conditions, but medical marijuana is legal in nearly half the states and doctors are increasingly studying its effects on various ailments. However, under federal law, marijuana is illegal to grow, sell or use for any purpose. This presents a Catch-22 as research is difficult to conduct due to tight restrictions.

Historian David Starkey has made controversial statements about ethnic minorities, disabled people, and women in an interview with the Daily Telegraph. He criticized Baroness Doreen Lawrence for treating minorities as victims and claimed women are of average intelligence. He also expressed his views on the current political class and the lack of talent in politics. Starkey, who identifies as gay and disabled, believes that all forms of liberation depend on individuals refusing to be victims. He also criticized the fear of Islamophobia and the portrayal of Muslims as victims. Starkey's comments have sparked controversy and criticism.

Barcelona forward Pedro is considering his future at Camp Nou and could join Liverpool if Raheem Sterling leaves Anfield. Pedro would command £90,000-a-week wages, less than Liverpool offered Sterling, and would cost less than the £50million Liverpool would receive for Sterling. Pedro has been looking for a starting place and Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers has scouted him. Barcelona cannot sign players until January 2016 but they will sell if the price is right. Alex Song will also be allowed to leave and Xavi Hernandez and Dani Alves are hoping to stay. Xavi wants to delay an announcement until the end of the season and Alves is hoping for a longer contract.

Newcastle United fans are planning to boycott the club's next home game against Tottenham in protest against owner Mike Ashley. A social media campaign has been launched to encourage fans to turn up in the lowest ever Premier League crowd and hold demonstrations before and after the game. A website, Sack Ashley.com, has been set up to promote the boycott and a visual and audible protest in Leazes Park. Newcastle boss John Carver suffered a fourth successive defeat at Sunderland on Sunday and the boycott and protests have also received the support of the Newcastle United Supporters Trust. The trust believes in supporter representation/ownership and has tried to engage the club for years to no avail. They support the action intended to bring about change in ownership of the club, particularly if it ultimately results in increased supporter representation/ownership.

Demi Moore is selling her Manhattan penthouse apartment, which she once shared with ex-husband Bruce Willis, for a record-breaking $75 million. The 14-bedroom apartment includes 7,000 square feet of living space, wrap-around terraces, and views of Central Park and the Hudson River. The couple purchased the apartment in 1990 and decorated it in a Southwestern mission motif. They split up in 2000, and Moore no longer spends much time there. The San Remo building was designed in 1929 and turned into a co-op in 1972. Neighbors include Dustin Hoffman, Diane Keaton, Steven Spielberg, and U2 frontman Bono. The combined monthly maintenance fees for both residences are over $20,000. Moore is selling the apartment and maisonette since she doesn't spend much time there anymore. Adam D Modlin, president of the Modlin Group, is in charge of the listing and says there is no other apartment in the neighborhood to rival Moore's. The couple was married from 1987 until 2000 and share three daughters.

McDonald's announced plans to raise wages for its employees working at company-owned restaurants in the US, starting July 1. The average wage is expected to be more than $10 an hour by the end of 2016. This move comes as part of an improving economy and public pressure to increase wages. McDonald's USA President Mike Andres stated that only a few employees participated in the protests and that the company wants to be the most competitive and attractive employer. In addition to wage increases, McDonald's will also offer paid time off for employees who have worked for the company for at least a year and work an average of 20 hours a week. McDonald's US business has been struggling, with sales and customers counts at established locations falling two years in a row. The company named Steve Easterbrook as its new CEO in January, and the change took effect last month. McDonald's also plans to expand benefits to help workers at company- and franchise-owned restaurants complete high school and college.

Over 1,700 Chinese students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province took their exams in the playground of their high school due to lack of indoor space. The students suggested and organized the outdoor exam themselves, and took measures to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school approved the proposal as a test of the students' organizing capacity and to broaden their horizons. Some students also believed it could help prevent cheating. The students found the experience to be relaxing and a novel way to broaden their horizons.

Inter Milan are in talks with Manchester City about signing forward Stevan Jovetic, who looks set to leave the Etihad this summer. City are unwilling to let him go on loan but are open to offers for a permanent transfer. Inter are also interested in a deal for Yaya Toure and veteran midfielder Toure could be one of several players to leave the Premier League champions this summer. Inter boss Roberto Mancini is hoping to sign both players but it won't be easy. Jovetic was omitted from City's Champions League squad earlier this season to make room for Wilfried Bony. Inter rejected several bids from City last summer and Juventus showed interest in the Montenegro star during the last transfer window. City are willing to listen to offers for Jovetic if they can recoup a significant amount of the £22million they paid Fiorentina for him in 2013. Inter are unlikely to turn Lukas Podolski's loan move from Arsenal into a permanent one.

Patrick James Fredricksen, a 30-year-old known child sex offender, was arrested in Utah on suspicion of stealing a school bus and attempting to abduct young children. He had previously used the bus's on-board list of children's names and addresses to try and abduct a young girl. Fredricksen had been working at a baseball complex when he allegedly stole a funeral-parlor worker's car and used it to steal a school bus. He was stopped by a sheriff's lieutenant after attempting to pick up a child at her home. Fredricksen is on Utah's Sex Offender Registry and has previous convictions for unlawful sexual activity with a minor, sexual exploitation of a minor, dealing in material harmful to a minor, and impersonating a firefighter. He had previously worked as a volunteer firefighter but was dismissed for stealing clothing and equipment and impersonating a firefighter. He was sentenced to 36 months of probation and ordered to have counselling. Fredricksen is currently in jail for investigation of theft of a vehicle and attempted child kidnapping, and is also expected to face a charge of damaging a prison.

Former U.S. Marine Charlie Linville, who lost his right leg and several fingers in an explosion in Afghanistan, is attempting to climb Mount Everest for the second time to inspire others. He is using a specially designed metal foot with a climbing boot and crampons to conquer the 8,850-meter (29,035-foot) summit next month. Linville, who is retired from the military and has been climbing with The Heroes Project since 2013, was stopped last year due to the deaths of 16 Sherpa guides in an avalanche. He plans to approach from the northern, Tibetan side this time with an eight-member team. Linville said his message is that anything is possible and anyone can overcome life's challenges with determination. He lost his leg and fingers in an explosion in Afghanistan in 2011.

Liana Barrientos, a 39-year-old woman from New York, is facing criminal charges for allegedly participating in an immigration scam by getting married 10 times between 1999 and 2010. She is currently charged with two counts of offering a false instrument for filing in the first degree for falsely stating it was her "first and only" marriage in her 2010 application. Prosecutors believe the scam involved some of her husbands, who filed for permanent residence status shortly after the marriages, and any divorces happened only after the filings were approved. It is unclear if any of the men will be prosecuted. Barrientos is believed to still be married to four men and was arrested for theft of service and criminal trespass after leaving court. If convicted, she faces up to four years in prison and her next court appearance is scheduled for May 18.

Mauricio Pochettino believes Harry Kane should win the PFA Player of the Year award over Eden Hazard due to his impact on English football. Kane has been nominated for the award after scoring 29 goals for Tottenham this season. Pochettino also defended the club's decision to play a one off pre-season game against the MLS All Stars in Colorado. The game is only one game and the team will only be away for three days. Pochettino also mentioned that the team will be playing against some of the biggest stars in the world, making it a good test for the team. Kane and Hazard are the leading contenders for the award with Diego Costa, Alexis Sanchez, David de Gea, and Philippe Coutinho also nominated.

A 66-year-old man was arrested and charged with public nuisance and a breach of the peace after allegedly burning an Australian flag at the Shrine of Remembrance in Brisbane's Anzac Square on Friday afternoon. The incident occurred just days before Anzac Day commemoration services are to take place at the site, where tens of thousands are expected to gather to pay their respects to fallen service men and women. The man will face Brisbane Magistrate's Court on Saturday morning. This incident comes after veterans condemned protesters who burned the Australian flag at anti-Islamic and anti-racism protests in Melbourne. The RSL spokesperson stated that burning anyone's flag in anyone's country is not acceptable. Big screens have been set up around Anzac Square, Post Office Square, King George Square and Queen Street Mall to ensure that everyone attending the dawn service gets a glimpse of the moving service. Dawn services will start at 4.28am at the Shrine of Remembrance in Adelaide Street's Anzac Square.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini believes his team needs to make significant signings this summer in order to keep up with their rivals. City were hampered last summer by financial fair play regulations, resulting in a net spending cap of £49 million. Pellegrini has stated that his team needs to sign a "crack" player, such as striker Sergio Aguero, and has suggested this summer is the time to do it. Despite the team's current fourth place standing in the Premier League, Pellegrini still believes they are capable of retaining the title. He is focused on finishing the season strongly and has not yet discussed plans for next season. Pellegrini's comments could be seen as a plea for more spending, but he has not yet indicated whether such a move will be sanctioned. His immediate concern is the team's league position, as results elsewhere have seen them drop two places over the weekend. While Pellegrini has not given up on the title, he cannot even take the runners-up spot for granted. He is emphasizing the importance of finishing the season strongly.

Seattle Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman was devastated after his team lost the Super Bowl to the New England Patriots, but he quickly found joy in the birth of his son, Rayden, just four days later. Sherman has shared photos of his newborn on Instagram and has been named the NFC Defensive Player of the Year by the Kansas City Committee of 101. Despite the accolade, Sherman will undergo surgery to repair a torn ligament in his left elbow before returning to the field in August. The Seahawks will play the Denver Broncos in their first preseason game as they aim to make it to the Super Bowl for the third consecutive season.

A 29-year-old man named Pankaj Saw died after falling from a balcony in Macquarie Park while on the phone with his new wife in India. It is believed that the wooden railing gave way, causing him to fall three stories to his death. Saw was in Australia on a work visa and had been working in Sydney for some time. He had recently returned from India where he got married. Friends and colleagues remember him as a lively and energetic person. Investigators are looking into whether a structural fault contributed to the accident. The balcony's bracket, which attaches it to the wall, appears to have been installed incorrectly and may have been a factor in the collapse. The man's death has left his friends and colleagues in grief.

An autopsy has revealed that a teenager killed by police in Illinois on Saturday was shot twice in the back. Justus Howell, 17, was chased down the street by police responding to an argument before being shot. Witnesses heard an officer say they had shot the boy, but it is not known if an officer has been suspended while the shooting is investigated. The teenager, who had moved to the area from Wisconsin in February, wanted to be a surgeon. His mother described him as a young man who was fleeing from police when he was killed. The autopsy results also include pending toxicology results. The Zion police chief did not return calls seeking comment.

Robert Durst, a jailed millionaire and suspected murderer, pleaded not guilty to a new federal gun possession charge in court on Tuesday. Durst is also facing a murder charge in California and two weapons charges in Louisiana. He previously pleaded guilty to two federal gun charges in Pennsylvania in 2004, but his lawyers argue that those convictions do not make it illegal for him to carry a gun under Louisiana law. Durst is currently being held without bail in a state prison due to concerns of suicide risk. The hearing had an unusual moment when Durst asked who the prosecutor was. Durst's lawyers are currently discussing another federal matter regarding two FBI agents and a state trooper on an FBI task force being held in contempt of court for failing to appear at a hearing. Durst's lawyers claim that his arrest in New Orleans was timed to coincide with the conclusion of HBO's 'The Jinx' series. Authorities found a passport, a latex mask, a handgun, and marijuana in his room. Durst's lawyers argue that the room was searched illegally.

Wigan secured their first away win of the season with a 40-22 victory over Wakefield, thanks to a hat-trick from Joe Burgess. Wakefield gave debuts to several players but suffered injuries to Ian Kirke and Danny Washbrook. Wigan looked set to cruise to victory but were made to work hard by Wakefield, who scored four tries. Burgess completed his hat-trick late in the game to help Wigan climb to second place in the table. Wakefield remain rooted to the bottom of the table.

Josh Warrington easily defeated Dennis Tubieron in Leeds to win the vacant WBC International featherweight title. Warrington, who is billed as the next Ricky Hatton, was never in trouble but failed to deliver the stoppage that had looked likely. Warrington was bored by the end of the fight and admitted he wanted to gain experience. Tubieron, who had previously boxed at bantamweight and lightweight, was the smaller man and was content to fight on the back foot. Warrington finished the stronger and was awarded a landslide victory by the judges. Warrington is now unbeaten in 21 contests and is looking for a world title shot within the next 12 months.

A nine-year-old boy named Tate Ricks went missing after a boating accident in the St Johns River in Florida. The boat was hit by a wake, causing it to capsize, and Tate immediately went underwater. The man with him attempted to save him but was unsuccessful. Authorities are searching the river using sonar, thermal imaging, and divers. Tate was believed to not be wearing a life jacket and the search area includes the St Johns River from US-17 to Memorial Bridge to the north, and Pico Road to the south. The incident is being investigated as a boating accident and no foul play is suspected. Tate's family is staying positive and praying for his safe return. He is described as a fun-loving kid who liked hunting, fishing, and NASCAR. The search operation will continue as long as conditions are safe.

An Albuquerque man, Sergio Barrientos-Hinojosa, allegedly opened fire at a customer he argued with at a gas station and used his 13-year-old son as a getaway driver. No one was injured, but police arrested Barrientos-Hinojosa later that night. He reportedly fired several gunshots during the incident and was yelling racial slurs at the officers. The son was reportedly shell-shocked and Barrientos-Hinojosa is facing charges including child abuse. It is unclear if he has an attorney. The incident occurred at a gas station in Albuquerque.

Kevin Carr, a British athlete from Devon, has set a new world record by becoming the fastest man to run around the world. He completed the 16,300-mile journey in 621 days, one day faster than the previous record held by Australian Tom Denniss. Carr ran a marathon a day every day for almost two years, crossing 26 countries and getting through 16 pairs of shoes. He encountered various challenges such as bears, wild dogs, and extreme weather conditions. He was also the first man to complete the challenge unsupported, pushing all of his equipment in a stroller that weighed twice as much as he does. Carr's journey took him through Australia, New Zealand, Europe, India, the US, and Canada. He faced various dangers such as bears, wolves, and heatstroke, and was once hit by a car. Despite the challenges, Carr completed his journey and said that the highlight was running through the Andes mountains. He lost three stone during the trip and faced indifference from people on the road. Carr's journey took him to various locations around the world, from Alabama to Chile.

A Georgia middle school teacher, Nancy Perry, has been removed from the classroom and will retire after she expressed her critical personal opinion of President Barack Obama to students. Perry allegedly told students that Obama is a Muslim and that any parent who supports him couldn't be Christian. A parent, Jimmie Scott, complained to the school after his 12-year-old son brought the matter to his attention. During a parent-teacher conference, Perry and her husband showed Scott what he described as anti-Obama internet propaganda. Superintendent Chuck Ledbetter apologized to the student and his parents and stated that school principals are now required to call the superintendent if any board member asks to sit in on parent-teacher meetings. Scott also addressed the community at the meeting, stating that his family had been ridiculed and had racial slurs thrown at them. Perry's husband, who sits on the county Board of Education, should not have attended the parent-teacher conference.

Sunderland star Adam Johnson has been charged with grooming and three counts of sexual activity with a 15-year-old girl. He is due to appear in court on May 20 and faces a lengthy prison term if found guilty. Sunderland are under pressure to suspend Johnson, who could miss the club's remaining six games if suspended. Johnson was suspended by the club after his arrest but was later reinstated and has featured as a substitute in the last three matches. Johnson is accused of four offences under the Sexual Offences Act 2003 and is due to appear in court on May 20. The CPS has warned against reporting or commenting on the case to avoid prejudicing the proceedings. Sunderland travel to Stoke tomorrow and are just a point above the Premier League drop zone.

A 35-year-old man, James Webster, was spared jail after admitting outraging public decency by using a hidden camera to film up women's skirts in a Lidl store in Maidenhead, Berkshire. He was caught after a shopper noticed him moving his bag closer to a woman. Security guards discovered a hole in the bag through which he placed the lens of the camera. He admitted the offence and was warned that he could face prison but was instead given a three-year community order and ordered to complete a sexual offences treatment programme. Webster had targeted women as they shopped in Lidl and had been smoking cannabis at the time of the incident. He immediately showed remorse and had been clean since the incident. The magistrate noted his early guilty plea and remorse but also his mature age and the fact that he had shown obvious intention. Webster was ordered to pay £85 in costs and a £60 fine.

A man from New Zealand, Matthew Bird, drastically reduced his income by quitting his well-paid job to become a mechanic in order to avoid a significant increase in his child support payments. The change in Inland Revenue's child support formula resulted in an increase of $600 a month for Bird, from $1,300 to $1,900. He believes the increased figure is unreasonable and that illegal employment may flourish under the new system. Another man, Dean Sorenson, also faces financial difficulty due to the increase in his child support payments by $172 a month. MP Jo Goodhew has invited parents to her office to discuss how the new calculations are affecting their wages and to provide assistance. Inland Revenue has advised parents to check the information they provided to ensure their payments have been calculated correctly. Two inquiries about the changes to child support payments have been received by Waitaki MP Jacqui Dean's office.

Newcastle United manager John Carver has criticized Moussa Sissoko for his reckless tackle on Liverpool midfielder Lucas, which resulted in a red card for the Newcastle captain. Carver admitted that the tackle could have been a straight red and expressed his disappointment over the referee's decision not to award a penalty to Ayoze Perez. Despite the defeat, Carver saw some positives in his team's performance and felt that they held their own against Liverpool. Sissoko could face disciplinary action for his tackle.

Manchester City is currently leading the Premier League, but they are vulnerable to being overtaken by Liverpool in the remaining six matches. City's performance this season has been poor, and they have failed to identify suitable replacements for players such as Yaya Toure and Samir Nasri. City's long-term plan is to bring in Pep Guardiola, but if they are caught and condemned to the Europa League, their financial capacity to improve would be limited, and it is uncertain if Guardiola would come under those circumstances. City's recent signings such as Jesus Navas, Martin Demichelis, and Fernandinho have not lived up to expectations. City's powers that be are waiting for Guardiola to leave Bayern Munich for Manchester, but what if City is caught and condemned to the Europa League? The financial fair play regulations could limit City's capacity to improve, and it is uncertain if Guardiola would come under those circumstances. City's recent performance has been weak, and keeping Pellegrini on another year while marking time for Guardiola is a giant gamble. Roberto Mancini got City into the elite in the nick of time with the financial fair play regulations about to be introduced, and City's capacity to improve would be severely limited if they are caught and condemned to the Europa League.

Manny Pacquiao's May 2 megafight against Floyd Mayweather has led to a surge in sales of Pacquiao-related merchandise in the Philippines. Retailers are struggling to keep up with demand for T-shirts, boxing gloves, figurines, caps, and jackets, with buyers hoping to make a profit if Pacquiao wins. Prices for Pacquiao-autographed boxing gloves have risen at least 50%, and sales via Ebay have jumped 10 times. Even street vendors are making a profit selling lower-priced Pacquiao T-shirts. Pacquiao is widely regarded as a national idol in the Philippines, and thousands of fans are expected to watch the fight on large LED screens throughout Manila. Pacquiao is seen as the underdog, but his followers are confident he will win.

Novak Djokovic apologized for losing his temper and scaring a ball boy during the Miami Open final against Andy Murray. Djokovic shouted at his team and grabbed a towel from the ball boy, who was standing between him and his team during the heated exchange. Djokovic expressed regret for the incident and apologized to the boy and his parents. He also acknowledged that as a father, he wouldn't wish the same thing on his son. Djokovic was feeling the pressure after Murray fought back from a first set tie-break loss to win the second set in the blazing heat of Key Biscayne, Florida. But the outburst seemed to give Djokovic the boost he needed to win the third set 6-0 and claim his fifth Miami Open title. Djokovic was seen relaxing on the beach with his dogs after the win.

Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao's highly anticipated boxing match in Las Vegas next month will bring in an estimated $400m in revenue. The referee for the fight will earn $10,000, with Kenny Bayless and Tony Weeks being the frontrunners. Both fighters are in the final stages of their preparations for the May 2 bout. Pacquiao's trainer Freddie Roach has asked for a fair referee for the fight. Both boxers are in good shape and are close to the welterweight limit. Pacquiao has been training in Los Angeles and has been showcasing his skills to the public. Mayweather has already revealed that he is close to the limit. The referee for the fight is yet to be announced.

Roma ended their four-month winless streak at home by defeating Napoli in Serie A on Saturday. Miralem Pjanic scored the only goal of the match in the 25th minute and goalkeeper Morgan de Sanctis made several saves in the second half to secure the victory. Roma moved four points ahead of Lazio, while Napoli's winless streak was extended to five matches. Security was tight for the match due to fan violence in the past. Roma was without injured captain Francesco Totti and fellow forward Gervinho, but Pjanic made an impact with a free kick from 30 meters that sailed just wide of the post. Roma full back Jose Holebas tracked Napoli midfielder Jose Callejon as Roma finally won at home. Napoli may have had a case for a penalty, but there wasn't much of a protest. In the second half, De Sanctis was superb in denying Dries Mertens on several occasions and made a leaping save on a shot from Manolo Gabbiadini in the 64th. Napoli forward Lorenzo Insigne came on late for his first action since tearing his knee in November.

The parents of the youngest victim of the Boston Marathon bombings are urging the Justice Department to drop the death penalty for the man convicted in the case. In an opinion piece in The Boston Globe, Bill and Denise Richard described the toll the death of their 8-year-old son, Martin, and injuries to their daughter, Jane, have taken on their family. They understand the heinousness of the crimes committed but are asking for the defendant, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, to spend the rest of his life in prison without the possibility of release and waiving all of his rights to appeal. They hope this will bring an end to the anguish and allow their family and the city of Boston to move forward. Tsarnaev was convicted last week, while his brother, Tamerlan, was killed in a shootout with police two years ago. The Richards never mention Tsarnaev by name and stress that they are only speaking for themselves.

According to a study by YouGov, people with the name Nigel are twice as likely to vote for Ukip compared to the general population. The study also found that certain names are more likely to vote for the Conservative, Labour, and Liberal Democrat parties. For example, the names Charlotte, Fiona, and Pauline are more likely to vote Conservative, while Sharon, Samantha, and Clare are less likely. The study comes after a Ukip election candidate was investigated for providing sausage rolls to voters, which is against Electoral Commission rules. The candidate, Kim Rose, denies any wrongdoing.

A headteacher, David Nicholson, from The Costello School in Basingstoke, Hampshire, has resigned after allegedly using his school email to arrange a threesome with a prostitute. He reportedly sent explicit messages to the woman, expressing his desire for her to dress up as a schoolgirl and be spanked. The investigation by Ofsted is ongoing, and Mr. Nicholson is still under investigation. He is also training to be an Ofsted inspector and has previously worked as a headteacher in Chippenham, Wiltshire. The school's chair of governors, Carol Bode, confirmed the board's acceptance of Mr. Nicholson's resignation and stated that there are no concerns related to the safeguarding of pupils. The school is now being led by Mr. Leigh Adams, the acting headteacher. Mr. Nicholson is married with four children.

An 83-year-old man named Thomas Cain was surprised with a long-lost photograph of his mother, Ora Mae, who died when he was 13. His granddaughter, Andrea Ferrell, had been searching for photographs of her ancestors for two years and finally found this one with a distant relative in Florida. When Thomas saw the photograph, he was shocked and emotional, and asked where it came from. Ferrell explained that she had found it with a relative and was thrilled to be able to give this gift to her beloved grandfather. Thomas's family described him as the greatest, most humble, God-fearing, family-oriented, loving man in the world. Ferrell is still searching for photographs of Thomas's father, Henry, who also died young.

Honest is a new app that allows users to ask personal questions anonymously and receive feedback from other anonymous users. The app was created by two London advertising executives and aims to provide unbiased opinions and advice from a global society. Users can ask questions about relationships, sexual dysfunction, career changes, and secret crushes, among other topics. The app harnesses the power of "collective intelligence" and removes social norms to provide honest and truthful advice. Examples of questions include "My long term girlfriend is bad in bed...shall I tell her?" and "Shall I tell my girlfriend I hired a prostitute?" Honest can be downloaded for free on iOS.

Chicago Cubs fans experienced long wait times and had to use plastic cups as makeshift toilets during opening day at Wrigley Field due to only two working bathrooms. The modernization of the stadium caused a public health disaster and the Cubs apologized for the inconvenience. Thousands of fans were affected and social media was flooded with complaints. The Cubs plan to add portable units and monitor wait times to improve the situation.

A study by The Tab, a student newspaper, found that students studying computer science and dentistry at British universities are less likely to have had sex than those in other subjects. Eleven percent of computer scientists, nine percent of physicists, five percent of dentists, and four percent of law, chemistry, engineering and medicine students reported being virgins. In contrast, only one percent of students in Arts subjects like history and English reported being virgins. The survey also found that the average number of sexual partners for university students in Britain is 8.2. The survey revealed that 22 percent of students didn't lose their virginity until they were 18, 19 percent lost their virginity at 17, and 15 percent lost their virginity just before the age of consent - at 15. A shocking 1.66 percent of students revealed they first had sex when they were 13 years of age or younger. The student newspaper also compiled a list of universities where people lost their virginity earliest, with seven percent of people following Aston and Ulster universities. Meanwhile, one in ten students from Lancaster University and nine percent from both Kent and Royal Holloway University reported still being virgins.

Sam Allardyce is unsure if he will be the manager of West Ham next season as his contract expires at the end of the season and his future with co-owners David Gold and David Sullivan is uncertain. West Ham have had a poor run of form in 2015, leading to speculation that Allardyce will be let go. He is already making plans for next season and has a meeting planned with the co-owners at the end of May to discuss his position. West Ham currently sit on 42 points from 31 games and face Stoke City on Saturday. Allardyce will attempt to lead West Ham back to form.

A giraffe named Katie at the Dallas Zoo gave birth to a baby giraffe in a live stream event captured by 10 cameras and broadcasted by Animal Planet. The labor lasted for an hour and the baby was about 6 feet tall. The gender and condition of the newborn were not immediately known but there were good signs such as the baby's ears moving, standing, and nursing. Katie is described as a "diva" among the herd of 12 giraffes at the zoo and is known for her spunky behavior. The baby joins a 4-year-old sister Jamie and had watchers in the form of fellow giraffes. The labor was a long time coming as giraffes have a 15-month gestation period on average. It is not known how many people watched the event online.

Aldi opened a new store in Avlaston, Derbyshire, and gave away prizes to the first 100 customers. Over 200 people queued overnight to get their hands on deals, including a 21.5inch television. The store will create 29 jobs and has a car park. Aldi donated £250 to the council and children's treats to Alvaston Children's Centre. Former Derby County player Craig Ramage cut the ribbon and the store is one of 60 opening across the UK this year.

A fight broke out in downtown Orlando, Florida involving 'multiple individuals'. Britney E. Montenegro, a 20-year-old woman from Queens, New York was arrested after trying to attack another woman. She was covered in blood, but it was not her own. Montenegro was charged with disorderly conduct and was relatively unscathed despite the injury. The incident occurred at East Pine Street and South Court Avenue around 2.40 am. Montenegro attends Valencia Community College and works at Bayhill Eyecare and Eyewear. Police are still investigating the incident.

Everton manager Roberto Martinez defended Ross Barkley's decision to take a penalty instead of Leighton Baines despite Baines' successful record. Barkley's effort was saved but Everton went on to win 1-0. Martinez argued that Barkley had the right to take the penalty and that he was happy to have multiple players who could take penalties. Barkley's penalty was well-struck but saved by Burnley goalkeeper Tom Heaton. Mirallas scored the only goal of the game after 29 minutes. In January, Mirallas took a penalty from Baines and missed. Martinez was happy with Barkley's responsibility in taking the penalty.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a giant omelette containing 150 eggs and 12,000 calories for Easter. The omelette, which is three-foot in circumference and contains 945g of protein, is recommended for a group of no fewer than five people to eat. It took an hour to cook and contains almost five times the daily intake for a grown man. Ally recommends attempting to eat the omelette in a group.

Formula One legend Jackie Stewart has expressed concern over the decline of European races in the F1 calendar, specifically the German Grand Prix which was dropped from the 2015 schedule due to financial issues. F1 races have been moving towards lucrative venues in the Middle East, leading to a decrease in European races. Stewart, a three-time world champion, believes that essential races in Germany, Italy, Britain, France and Monaco should remain unchanged as they helped motorsport become what it is today. The Italian Grand Prix is also in doubt due to financial problems. F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone has not been able to guarantee the future of the Italian Grand Prix. The German Grand Prix was erased from the schedule due to a lack of agreement between the commercial rights holder and the promoter. The decision has resulted in a shortened 2015 season with 19 races.

A middle school teacher in New York was assaulted by a student's mother and her niece after the mother believed the teacher had put her hands on her daughter. The incident occurred at Alverta B. Gray Schultz Middle School in Hempstead, and the teacher, Catherine Engelhardt, was shoved against the wall, placed in a headlock, and thrown to the floor. Several students were also involved in the attack. Engelhardt was unconscious for several minutes and rushed to the hospital. She has since been released and is recovering at home. The attack was caught on the school's security cameras, and the mother, Annika McKenzie, and her niece were arrested and charged with second-degree assault on school grounds and second-degree strangulation. Engelhardt has previously expressed concerns about safety at the school.

A 24-year-old Syrian national and naturalized US citizen from San Diego, named Mohamad Saeed Kodaimati, was arrested and charged with lying to federal agents about his involvement with Islamic State militants in Syria. He is accused of making false statements during interviews with the FBI and other US authorities at the US Embassy in Ankara, Turkey, in March. The FBI has found evidence to the contrary, including incriminating Facebook photos and posts indicating his alleged involvement with Syrian militants. Saeed falsely claimed he had not been involved in any fighting, had never fired his weapon at anyone and did not know any Islamic State members. He also claimed he had never told anyone he was involved with the Nusra Front and had never worked or volunteered at a Sharia court. Federal agents have uncovered evidence of Saeed's alleged involvement with Syrian militants, including a photo of him with a man who has sworn allegiance to ISIS, and posts and chats where he allegedly bragged about working for a sharia court, expressed his support for ISIS and claimed he had fought in a gun battle that lasted four months. Saeed traveled from San Diego to Istanbul and was in Syria and Turkey until his return to the United States in March. He was arrested Wednesday in Rancho Bernardo, located in the northern part of San Diego, and made his initial court appearance Thursday, where he was ordered held without bail. He is due back in court next Tuesday for a detention hearing.

Sheffield Wednesday claimed a 1-0 win over Brentford with Kieran Lee's second-half goal. Both teams played with high defensive lines, resulting in a low-scoring first half. The second half was more lively but produced few clear-cut chances. Wednesday had the best opportunity when Lee scored in the 75th minute. Brentford had a chance to equalize but Alan Judge missed an open goal. Harlee Dean made a costly mistake but could not lead to a goal for Wednesday. The win boosted Wednesday's chances of avoiding relegation while Brentford's promotion hopes suffered a blow.

A man named Carlos Colina, 32, is being held on $1 million bail after pleading not guilty to aggravated assault and battery, improper disposal of a human body, and other charges in connection to the death of his friend, Jonathan Camilien, 26. The remains of Camilien were found in a duffel bag near the Massachusetts Institute of Technology campus and his head was discovered in Colina's apartment building across the street. Colina had previously been kicked out of a gym for starting a fight over gym equipment and intimidating other gym users. He is believed to have known his alleged victim and has an outstanding assault and battery case pending from the November incident. No motive has been released and Colina is considered a homicide suspect, but no murder charges have been filed yet. A pretrial hearing has been scheduled for April 14.

Ferrari team principal Maurizio Arrivabene has urged Kimi Raikkonen to improve his performances if he wants to stay with the team beyond the current season. Raikkonen's contract expires at the end of the year, but there is an option for 2016 if both parties agree. Raikkonen has been happy working with the team, but his form has not been as good as team-mate Sebastian Vettel. Raikkonen has let himself down in qualifying, but has recovered well in the last two races to finish fourth. Arrivabene has told Raikkonen that his results need to improve if he wants to stay with Ferrari. Raikkonen has shown he has the speed and appears keen on staying, but Arrivabene has made it clear that results are the most important factor. Raikkonen and Maldonado had a heated moment during practice in Bahrain. Raikkonen has been told to push and knows that his performance is key to his future with Ferrari.

A New Zealand hunter, Max Verschuuren, is lucky to be alive after his friend mistook him for a deer and shot him in the back with a .270 rifle. Verschuuren was bent over emptying rocks out of his boot on his way to a felled deer in the Te Urewera forest when his friend shot him. He tumbled down the hill in an attempt to escape any further bullets and kept his cool until he was carried over to the rest of the hunting party. The friend who shot him was mortified and has visited Verschuuren every day in the hospital. Verschuuren has received stitches and is expected to be discharged from the hospital later on Monday. Local police are investigating the incident and have issued a warning to hunters to take appropriate safety measures. Verschuuren has pledged to continue shooting, even with the friend who shot him.

A family in Washington was horrified to discover that their baby monitor had been hacked, with a stranger able to control the audio and camera to spy on their three-year-old son. The parents had initially put their son's complaints of someone talking to him at night down to an over-active imagination, but one night they heard a man's voice come over the monitor saying 'Wake up little boy, daddy's looking for you'. The family believes the stranger had also hacked the camera, and had been able to remotely control it to watch the family. Technology experts have warned that it is becoming easier for hackers to infiltrate family's baby monitors as many of the newer devices connect to the internet. Parents are advised to change the passwords on the devices to make it more difficult for people to guess. Earlier this month, another family in Minnesota discovered their baby monitors and cameras had been infiltrated after they found footage from the nanny cam posted online. The family had first become suspicious after they heard music coming from their baby's room. The hacker had been able to access footage from baby monitors all over the world. Experts warn that parents should be aware of the potential risks of having internet-connected baby monitors in their homes.

New York Mayor Bill de Blasio is holding off on endorsing Hillary Clinton for president until he sees a clear vision of where she plans to go with her campaign and how she plans to address income inequality. De Blasio, who was Clinton's campaign manager in her successful 2000 Senate run, said it is important for her to define her campaign message and present a progressive vision. He noted that income inequality in the U.S. is "out of control" and needs to be addressed. De Blasio said Clinton's successful efforts to listen to everyday people during her 2000 Senate run will be necessary this year as Americans are still hurting from the Great Recession. He believes Clinton has a tremendous opportunity to present a progressive vision this year.
