A bearded dragon named Liz is gaining attention for her apparent understanding of the English language. In a video, owner Shannen Hussein asks Liz if she's hungry and the reptile responds with a nod of her head. Liz is rewarded with a superworm treat for her conversational skills. Liz isn't the only pet of Shannen's to gain internet fame, her pet lamb Winter is also popular online. Shannen also cares for two cats, two birds, a snake, and a number of ducklings, as well as turtles, a llama, and an emu. Liz seems to love superworms and will do anything to get one. After her meal, Liz sits back looking satisfied.

Esteban Cambiasso, a former Argentina international and five-time Serie A champion with Inter Milan, has said that helping Leicester City avoid relegation from the Premier League would be one of the highlights of his career. Cambiasso joined Leicester last summer on a free transfer and signed a one-year deal. Leicester, who were promoted last season, are currently at the bottom of the table and without a league win since January. Cambiasso believes that the team still has a chance to stay in the Premier League and is confident that they can do so. He has also won the Champions League with Inter Milan and represented Argentina 52 times, scoring five goals. Leicester will face West Ham United at home on Saturday.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers believes his team's recent defeats are due to their own failings rather than opponents figuring out their system. After an impressive 13-match unbeaten run, Liverpool's performances have dropped and they have lost ground in the race for the Champions League places. Rodgers insists that the team needs to create more chances and take them, and that it's his job to find solutions. Liverpool face Blackburn in the FA Cup quarter-final replay on Wednesday, and Rodgers is determined to reach the semi-finals in the cup competitions. Blackburn, who have dispatched top-flight sides Swansea and Stoke at Ewood Park, will be putting all their efforts into reaching a Wembley last-four encounter with Aston Villa.

The London Book Fair Author HQ event is a three-day programme offering informative seminars for aspiring authors. Experts from various publishing companies and organizations will share their knowledge and provide advice on getting published. Representatives from Little, Brown, HarperCollins, Quercus, The Creative Penn, The Alliance of Independent Authors, The Society of Authors, and agents David Higham Associates, The Agency Group, and A. M. Heath will be present. Experienced authors will share their career launching stories, and Kindle Direct Publishing authors will discuss their experiences in the e-book market. Seminars will focus on crime/thrillers and contemporary fiction genres, revealing what publishers and agents look for. There will also be a talk on crowdfunding and a Know Your Rights seminar. The London Book and Screen Week is running simultaneously, featuring hundreds of events across the capital. The London Book Fair is at its new venue, Olympia, West London, and seminars are free with a three-day LBF pass.

Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink led Burton Albion to promotion to League One for the first time in their history, but he is not content to stop there. After securing the championship medal, Hasselbaink and his team celebrated with champagne and are now aiming to finish the season as champions. The manager praised his predecessor Gary Rowett for laying the foundation for their success and expressed his desire to stay at the top. Burton Albion has two more games to prepare for and will train hard to achieve their goal. Hasselbaink also acknowledged Rowett's contribution to the club's achievements.

Japanese airline All Nippon Airways is set to unveil a new Boeing 787 Dreamliner decorated to look like the Star Wars character R2-D2. The plane will feature blue panels on the cockpit and front half of the white fuselage, as well as the words "Star Wars" in the movie's distinctive font. The trailer for the seventh installment of the Star Wars franchise, "The Force Awakens," was also released, featuring aerial dogfights and appearances by Han Solo and Chewbacca. Fans in the US and UK were treated to a livestream of the Star Wars Celebration, which featured director JJ Abrams and cast members. The film is due for release in December.

Josh Warrington will be accompanied into the ring by Vinnie Jones on Saturday during his boxing match in Leeds. Warrington is quickly becoming one of Britain's best-supported fighters and is aiming for a world title in the next 12 months. Other celebrities who have accompanied boxers into the ring include Justin Bieber and Lil Wayne with Floyd Mayweather, Liam Gallagher with Ricky Hatton, Prince Naseem Hamed with Puff Daddy, Nathan Cleverly with Mickey Rourke and Tom Jones, and Andrew Flintoff with Carl Frampton and Raul Hirales. These celebrities have added some sparkle to ring walks throughout the years.

PayPal is exploring the development of edible passwords that would be powered by stomach acid and include mini computers, according to a presentation by the company's top developer. The technology would allow users to log in without typing in a password or using fingerprint scanning. Other possibilities include ingestible or injectable passwords, as well as vein recognition technologies and heartbeat recognition bands. However, PayPal later clarified that the comments were meant as blue skies thinking and that the company has no immediate plans to develop edible passwords. The company is currently working on fingerprint scanning and one-touch payments to make payments safer and easier for customers. The presentation also mentioned a new app called True Key that uses facial recognition to log in to password-protected websites instead of using a password. Security experts have long criticized the ease with which passwords can be broken and the average person's difficulty in remembering multiple passwords.

Real Madrid forward Gareth Bale suffered a calf strain after just two minutes of their league game against Malaga and is unlikely to recover in time for the second leg of the Champions League against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday. Bale, who has been injury-free since October, was forced off and Cristiano Ronaldo was the first to console him. Bale's absence will be a blow for Real Madrid as he has been in good form this season and scored in the finals last season. The team won the game against Malaga 3-1 in his absence. Bale's further tests will be conducted in the next 24 hours and his chances of recovering in time for the Champions League semi-final on May 5-6 are slim. Real Madrid will have to rely on their four-man midfield of Luka Modric, James Rodriguez, Toni Kroos and Isco with Ronaldo and Karim Benzema up front in Bale's absence.

Swansea manager Garry Monk is determined to stop his former manager Roberto Martinez from getting a win at his old stomping ground, the Liberty Stadium, on Saturday. Everton have had a tough season and have only avoided relegation by winning their last three matches. Swansea have never beaten Everton in the league but they claimed a point at Goodison Park in November after being reduced to 10 men. Martinez criticized Swansea's tactics that day but Monk believes it was more frustration from Martinez's own side. Swansea are looking to get their best Premier League points total of 47 by getting all three points against Everton. Monk holds no ill feeling towards Martinez and knows that Europe has had an impact on Everton's results. Everton have had to balance their domestic commitments with a demanding Europa League campaign. Swansea have maintained their impressive form and are looking to get their first win against Everton in the league. Monk believes that Everton will want to finish the season strongly and is hoping to continue their form against his former team.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar was rescued by security after jumping into a lions' enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. Kumar, who was drunk, ran towards the animals shouting that he would kill them. Security guards were able to rescue him before he reached the lions, as he fell into a moat. Kumar later explained that he was drunk and thought he had a good chance against the predators. Police cautioned him and sent him for psychiatric evaluation. Last year, a 20-year-old man was killed by a tiger in Delhi after entering its enclosure at the city zoo.

Real Housewives of New Jersey star Joe Giudice has had his driving license suspended for two years and was fined $10,000 by a state judge for having the worst driving record ever seen. He pleaded guilty to unlawful use of an ID and impersonation and is currently serving an 18-month sentence for bankruptcy fraud. His wife Teresa is also serving a 15-month sentence. The judge called Giudice's disrespect for the law into question and refused to lower the fine despite his lawyer's argument that he is destitute. Giudice is expected to be deported once his prison term ends. He was recently paid $75,000 for prison photos and a tell-all interview. Prosecutors in Passaic County said Giudice used his brother's identity to obtain a driver's license while his own was suspended for driving while intoxicated in 2010. The Giudices pleaded guilty in the federal case in March 2014 and were ordered to pay restitution of over $400,000. Joe Giudice is an Italian citizen by birth who never became a U.S. citizen.

The greater adjutant stork is an endangered species that has made its home at the Boragaon landfill in India. Photographer Timothy Bouldry was drawn to the area by the stork and ended up documenting the lives of the 100 families who live and work there. The residents of the landfill make their living by searching for and selling recyclable materials, such as plastic, metal, and wires. They live in homes made of recycled materials and have no electricity or running water. Despite the difficult conditions, the people of Boragaon are content and have a strong sense of community and spirituality. Bouldry has been traveling the world for the past seven years photographing landfills and helping the people who live there. He finds humanitarian photo projects to be the most fulfilling and is currently living and working in Nicaragua. Bouldry's photography and humanitarian work can be followed on Facebook and Twitter.

American rapper Tyga visited Arsenal's Emirates Stadium with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Kieran Gibbs. Tyga posed for pictures and even dyed his hair red to show his support for the team. Oxlade-Chamberlain and Gibbs gave Tyga a No 52 Arsenal shirt with the rapper's hashtag printed on the back. Tyga, who is currently touring the UK, was delighted with the gift and is a fan of Arsenal. Oxlade-Chamberlain could return to action for Arsenal's game against Hull, while Gibbs is hoping to start ahead of Nacho Monreal. Tyga has been in the news for dating Kylie Jenner.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit has ruled that Asian-American rock band The Slants cannot trademark their name because it is considered disparaging to Asians. The band, which plays a type of grunge music called Chinatown Dance Rock, argued that the name was a healthy reappropriation of a term usually considered a slur and that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office violated their First Amendment rights by refusing to grant the trademark. However, the court ruled that there was evidence the term is offensive to people of Asian descent and that the refusal to federally register a trademark does not prevent the applicant from still using it. The case has parallels to the Washington Redskins' lawsuit against five Native Americans who successfully convinced the PTO to cancel the NFL team's trademarks because the name disparages Native Americans. The team is appealing the cancellation, and The Slants are likely to seek review of the decision by the full Federal Circuit court. The USPTO declined to comment.

Manchester City will face Crystal Palace's Glenn Murray, who has the best minutes-per-goal ratio in the Premier League this season, on Easter Monday. Murray has scored a goal every 91 minutes, while Harry Kane and Diego Costa are tied for the top spot with 19 goals each. Olivier Giroud and Papiss Cisse have also had strong seasons, despite injury and suspension. Chelsea has four players in the top 10, with Loic Remy and Didier Drogba having good minutes-per-goal ratios. Frank Lampard and Sergio Aguero have similar ratios, but Murray beats them all with a goal every 364 minutes. Murray has scored four goals for Palace this season.

Memories Gourmet Pizza Co., a small business in Wisconsin, has been mistaken for Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana, which made headlines for refusing to cater a same-sex wedding. This mistake led to angry comments and calls to protest, causing the owners to become unwilling participants in the national debate over Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act. Despite their attempts to clarify the situation, the owners are worried about the potential damage to their business.

Exeter, England is being called the "poshest" city in the UK after Monopoly game makers were unable to find a suitable location for the low-rent Old Kent Road space on the board. Despite thousands of suggestions for landmarks to fill the more expensive slots, no one has come forward with ideas for the brown sections of the board, which cost $60 in Monopoly money. Exeter has recently seen an influx of wealthy students and luxury developments, making it difficult to find a suitable location for the lower end of the board. Game-makers are now making a second appeal for recommendations for any Exeter landmark that can replace Old Kent Road.

A New York teacher, Madeline Luciano, was fired after an incident in which she allegedly allowed eighth grade students to write insulting words about a classmate on the blackboard. The teacher claims she was trying to teach the students to be kinder to each other and stop the bullying. The incident took place last June and the girl had been targeted by bullies before. The investigation revealed that the girl's bookbag had been hidden and the students shouted insults across the classroom. Ms Luciano is now taking legal action against the city's education department in an attempt to get her license back and return to work. She claims the exercise was never meant to go so far and she had reprimanded the student writing the nasty comments. Ms Luciano has been working for New York's education department since 2010.

A mother who saw crime scene photos of her daughter's body 40 years after she was murdered is seeking revenge. Marcia Ritter, 12, was raped and choked to death in 1975 and her body was found 33 days later. Her mother, Virginia Trimble Ritter, was advised against seeing the photos by her then-husband. Last year, she asked to see them and was shown them on a laptop by the lead investigator. The photos showed Marcia's body with vomit, hair pulled out, and blood on her scalp. She shouted, "If I had a gun I'd kill him!" Marcia's body was found near her home in a windowless garage with a child's wading pool and her cookie money was missing. The case was unsolved for 33 years until Jerome Sydney Barrett was arrested in 2006 and convicted of second-degree murder in 2009. He was sentenced to 44 years in prison. Ritter had previously declined to see the photos but now regrets her decision. She wants to see the photos again and seek revenge. Marcia's body was found 150 yards from her home with a neck bone fractured and her clothes matching the DNA of Barrett. He was 15 at the time of the crime and was living in Memphis when he was arrested. He had been in prison on sex charges between 1974 and 2002 except for about a year when Marcia disappeared. Minister for Communications Malcolm Turnbull will be featured on the front cover of GQ Australia in an eight-page interview. He confirmed rumors of his plans to run for Prime Minister if Tony Abbott had been toppled in February's leadership spill. Critics have accused him of fishing for votes, but Turnbull insists he is comfortable in his own skin. He has previously been featured in GQ in 2013, discussing his rise to politics and business moves that made him a millionaire. In the interview, Turnbull also talks about his childhood and political stance. Two years ago, he had ruled out challenging Abbott's leadership and trying for the top job himself.

A 14-year-old boy named Jack Cordero from Portland, Oregon, vomited in a Powell's bookstore in March, leaving a "gigantic" mess for the staff to clean up. Despite the inconvenience, Jack wrote a sincere apology letter and included a Ben & Jerry's gift card as a token of appreciation. The manager was touched by the gesture and her spirits were lifted. The letter and gift card went viral on social media, with many praising Jack's good manners and restoring faith in humanity. The manager, Jennifer Wicka, was impressed by Jack's actions and said that he is on his way to becoming a fantastic adult.
base_texts: Indonesian President Joko Widodo has confirmed that the executions of drug convicts Andrew Chan and Myuran Sukumaran are imminent, with all legal appeals yet to be concluded. The pair, along with eight other death row prisoners, are expected to face the firing squad once their appeals have been exhausted. Three of the other prisoners are still awaiting the results of their appeals. President Widodo stated that the executions would take place after the conclusion of all legal procedures, and that he would not interfere in the process. The Indonesian Attorney-General has indicated that the executions will not take place until after the Asian African conference being held in Jakarta this week. Chan and Sukumaran are currently in an isolated cell on Nusakambangan Island, where they have lodged a challenge with the Constitutional Court to have their death sentences overturned.

A heartfelt handwritten note from a passenger named "Bethanie" to an unnamed pilot, thanking him for safely bringing her home, has gone viral on Twitter. The letter was shared by pilot Jai Dillon, who was shown the note by a colleague. In the letter, Bethanie expresses her gratitude for being able to live in Spain while splitting her time with family in England. She also extends compassion and understanding in light of the recent Germanwings tragedy and the role of pilots in ensuring safety. The letter received an outpouring of emotion on Twitter, with many praising the pilot's role. The letter currently has over 3,700 shares and almost 3,000 favorites. The pilot, Jai Dillon, was unable to reveal the airline or flight number due to security reasons. The Germanwings crash last week, where pilot Andreas Lubitz deliberately crashed the plane, killing all 150 people on board, including three Britons, is still under investigation. Lubitz had therapy for suicidal tendencies before getting his pilot's license.

Japan's Defense Minister, Gen Nakatani, assured parliament that Japan has never been invaded by aliens and no government studies into extra-terrestrials are ongoing. The assurance came in response to a question from MP Antonio Inoki, who had asked about the dispatch of aircraft to meet extraterrestrial visitors and studies on aliens. Inoki had once reported seeing a mysterious flying object. The Air Self Defense Force scrambles fighter jets when unidentified flying objects are detected, but none have been found to have originated from outside Earth. In 2007, the Japanese government issued a statement denying the existence of unidentified flying objects from other planets, but former government spokesman Nobutaka Machimura and then-Defense Minister Shigeru Ishiba had expressed personal beliefs in the existence of UFOs controlled by alien life-forms.

The article reports on a survey by the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) which found that nearly half of headteachers have vacancies in English, maths, and science departments in secondary schools. The recruitment crisis is worsening, with some posts attracting only one or two applicants. London schools are experiencing the most difficulties, followed by the North West and East of England. Recruitment is also challenging for non-core subjects such as geography, design and technology, business studies, computer science, religious education, and modern foreign languages. Headteachers believe recruitment is more difficult than in previous years. The ASCL is calling for urgent action from the next government to address the crisis, including expanding school-led teacher training, developing a core curriculum for teaching degrees, and launching a campaign to attract new recruits.

A 41-year-old Indian salesman in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) could face up to seven years in prison and a fine of up to one million dirham (£186,000) for allegedly cursing Islam and the Prophet Mohammad on Facebook. The man, identified only as S.G., is accused of posting a derogatory status after watching a news bulletin about the war in Iraq last July. He initially claimed he received the offensive image over WhatsApp but later admitted to posting it on Facebook. The UAE considers blasphemy a serious criminal offense, and authorities routinely censor materials deemed offensive to Islam. The salesman failed to attend a court hearing on Monday, and the case was adjourned until April 27. In 2011, a British tourist ended up in court in Dubai for calling the Islamic prophet Mohammad a 'terrorist' during an argument in a shopping center.

A man named Marcin Wasniewski, 34, from Coventry, survived a car accident where his car crashed into the back of a lorry on the A444 with only minor injuries and cuts. The accident left the car with twisted metal and scattered debris, and emergency services were shocked to see the driver walk away unassisted. Paramedics described the car as having "literally embedded" itself into the back of the lorry. Marcin suffered a serious injury to his face and left arm but is currently volunteering at a Christian centre while he recovers. He believes his survival was not by luck but due to Jesus Christ watching over him. Paramedics stated that the outcome would have been fatal if the impact had been just a couple of inches closer to the driver or if there had been a passenger in the car.

An enormous European eagle owl has been terrorizing the Dutch town of Noordeinde for months, attacking locals and drawing in birdwatchers. The owl, which weighs around 6lbs and has a wingspan of up to 75cm, has been perching on people's heads for about a minute before flying off. Residents believe the bird may have escaped from an aviary and has learned to associate humans with food. The owl's unusual behavior has attracted twitchers from around the country, putting Noordeinde on the map. Photographer Menno Scheefer traveled 68km to the town to capture images of the owl. The European eagle owl is one of the largest species of owls and is found in various habitats, mostly in remote areas.

A 100-year-old man, Michael Juskin, from Bergen County, New Jersey, is accused of killing his 88-year-old wife, Rosalia, with an ax while she slept, before taking his own life with a knife. The incident occurred on Sunday night. The couple had a history of domestic issues, but a motive for the murder-suicide has not been determined. Neighbors, who had noticed an increase in police presence at the Juskins' home in recent years, were visibly upset upon learning of the incident. Michael Juskin is one of the oldest people ever to be accused of homicide. Rosalia was described as a "very sweet lady," and Michael was reportedly suffering from dementia and mental problems. The couple's daughter had asked her mother to move out due to her husband's instability. Police had been called to the home a few times in the past, but no further details were provided.

Sherrell Dillon, a former resident of Benefits Street and a single mother-of-two, has revealed that she is currently homeless but has still managed to secure a place in the Top Model of Colour competition. Dillion, who was featured on the hit Channel 4 series, says she feels happiness for her co-star White Dee, who has enjoyed significant success since the show. Dillion has been living in temporary accommodation in Handsworth following a mice infestation at her home. She has been pursuing a career in modeling for many years and hopes this competition will be her big break. Dillion posed for new photos in a white and orange dress and high heels, showcasing her long toned legs. She became homeless after the house she was living in became infested with mice, and she is now living in temporary accommodation while she finds a permanent home. The final of Top Model of Colour UK takes place on May 30, and previous winners have been signed by major modeling agencies and graced top magazines. The winner will receive a modeling contract, jewellery, clothes, and shoes, among other prizes.

A border guard was killed and 11 others were injured in a cross-border fire exchange between Saudi border troops and militants in Yemen's Asir region. This is the first reported military death for Saudi Arabia since they began airstrikes against rebels in Yemen. Houthi rebels seized the presidential palace in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden, and Yemeni special forces loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh arrived in an attempt to secure the city. U.S. Navy warships are patrolling off Yemen to search for suspicious shipping, including potential weapons shipments from Iran to the Houthi rebels. A Panamanian-registered cargo ship was inspected but found to be carrying only cement and construction materials. The situation in Aden is described as extremely fluid and complicated, with hospitals struggling to provide supplies and civilians trying to leave the country. Additionally, Al Qaeda fighters reportedly freed 270 prisoners from Yemeni prisons.

The Royal Bank of Scotland (RBS) reported a loss of £446 million for the first quarter of 2015, bringing its total losses since being bailed out by taxpayers to £50 billion. The loss includes provisions for fines, lawsuits, and compensation for mis-sold financial products. RBS also reported a £453 million restructuring charge, primarily due to the slump in the value of US premises. The loss is a setback for taxpayers, who own 80% of the bank, and comes at an awkward time for Chancellor George Osborne, who had hoped to highlight the return to profit of state-backed Lloyds as evidence of his government's success in fixing the banks bailed out during the financial crisis. RBS's former CEO, Fred Goodwin, was knighted for services to banking in 2004 but was stripped of his title in 2012. The loss wiped over £700 million off the value of RBS shares, and the TaxPayers' Alliance called for RBS to focus on the future rather than dealing with legacy issues. The Conservative Party has blamed the last Labour government for failing to regulate the banks adequately during its time in power.

Kenny Bayless, a highly experienced referee known for his large physical presence and unflappable personality, has been appointed to oversee the much-anticipated Mayweather vs. Pacquiao fight on May 2. The appointment is welcomed by both camps, with Pacquiao's promoter, Bob Arum, praising Bayless as the best referee in the world. Bayless has previously refereed fights involving both Mayweather and Pacquiao, including Mayweather's battle against Marcos Maidana and Pacquiao's knockout by Juan Manuel Marquez. The Nevada State Athletic Commission, aware of the high-profile nature of the fight, has also brought in respected judge Glenn Feldman from Connecticut to join Las Vegas residents Dave Moretti and Burt Clements as judges for the event. Bayless will receive $25,000 for the night's work, while the judges will each receive $20,000.

A Chinese hospital, Zheng Gong Hospital in Henan Province, is being moved eight meters a day to avoid demolition for a new road. The two-story brick outpatient building, which is 1,700 square meters in size, is being rolled on over 1,000 giant cylinder-shaped metal rollers. The move will take three days once prepared, but the preparation has already taken over a month. This is not the first time engineers in China have moved a building using rollers; a six-story building in Shanghai was moved 38 meters in 2013, and the Fu Gang Building in Guangxi Province was moved 36 meters in 2004. Both of these buildings also hold records in the Guinness Book of Records for the largest buildings moved in this way.

Martin Odegaard, a 16-year-old Norwegian midfielder playing for Real Madrid's Castilla team, met and was starstruck by former Brazil international and Real Madrid legend Ronaldo during the latter's visit to the training ground. Odegaard joined Real Madrid in January for £2.3 million and signed a long-term contract worth £40,000 a week. He has been training regularly with the first team, but was recently dropped from the Castilla side due to poor results. Some team-mates reportedly feel that Odegaard's frequent training with the first team makes him less cohesive in the B team. Real Madrid is desperate for the Castilla side to be promoted to the second tier of Spanish football, and first team coach Zinedine Zidane must decide whether to keep Odegaard in the B team or allow him to continue training with the first team.

A woman named Margaret Hesketh, 70, passed away in the Royal Albert Edward Infirmary in Wigan in November 2014. Her family claims that doctors wrongly diagnosed her with terminal cancer and put her on a Liverpool Care Pathway-style treatment for the dying, which included having her fluid and nutrition drips removed. However, a post-mortem examination found no evidence of cancer, and she was actually suffering from pneumonia and malnutrition at the time of her death. The family is calling for a criminal investigation and is planning to bring this up at an inquest this week. The hospital has stated that they cannot provide more details due to patient confidentiality but will provide a more balanced view of events during the inquest. The hospital also confirmed that they stopped using the Liverpool Care Pathway in July 2014.

Barcelona players Neymar, Dani Alves, and Adriano were delighted after their team's important win over Celta Vigo in La Liga, despite their questionable denim outfits. The trio all started and played crucial roles in the victory, which saw Barcelona return to the top of the table. Center-back Jeremy Mathieu scored the winning goal, but admitted his side struggled throughout the match due to the international break. Mathieu praised Gerard Pique for his impressive defensive display and praised the team for securing the three points. Dani Alves, who is being linked with a move away from Barcelona, also posted about the win on social media.

Aydian Ethan Dowling, a transgender man, is leading the Men's Health Magazine's Ultimate Guy Search with a significant vote margin. He has around 40,000 votes, surpassing his closest competitor by 30,000. The competition aims to find a man who embodies the qualities of today's well-rounded, active, health-conscious, and thoughtful guy. Aydian, who transitioned in 2009, lives in Oregon with his wife Jenilee. He is a role model for many, with a large following on Facebook, and has launched his own sportswear brand, Point5cc, to highlight transgender pride. Aydian's application emphasizes his struggle to find peace within his soul and his love for hiking and being outdoors. If he wins, he would make history as the magazine's first transgender cover star. The public vote counts for only 10% of the total, but Aydian is confident that he can win over the judging panel. He would follow Iraq war veteran and amputee Noah Galloway, who won the top spot last year.

Manchester Airport temporarily suspended flights after a reported drone sighting, causing disruption for hundreds of travellers. All flights were halted for about 20 minutes, and some were delayed or diverted while police searched the area. No evidence of a drone was found, and flights resumed. Drone sightings near airports have become a serious problem due to their increasing popularity and potential danger to commercial aircraft. The Civil Aviation Authority has successfully prosecuted two drone operators for safety breaches. Drones cannot be flown beyond the operator's line of sight, must be kept a safe distance from people and structures, and cannot be flown near congested areas or large groups of people.

This article discusses the evolution of YouTube as a platform for content creation and consumption, with a focus on its impact in Japan. The article highlights the 10-year anniversary of the first video uploaded on YouTube, and the site's growth into a major player in the media industry. YouTube is investing in "YouTube Spaces" to provide resources and professional studios for independent creators, breaking down barriers for low-budget productions. The article features the filming of a new sci-fi horror movie, "The Crawler in the Dark," which will be released directly on YouTube. The article also mentions the popularity of YouTube channels, with examples of successful creators like PewDiePie, and partnerships with traditional media companies like Toei to encourage more high-quality content and attract new subscribers. The article concludes by noting the financial rewards that can come from a viral video, with some creators earning six-figure incomes or even millions of dollars.

Sutherland Council in Sydney is considering allowing overseas backpackers to camp in allocated areas on popular beaches, such as Cronulla and Wanda, to encourage tourism and boost the local economy. The proposal was made by Councillor Steve Simpson, who believes that providing a legal camping site would solve the issue of illegal parking on streets and encourage spending in local businesses. However, some locals have expressed negative responses to the idea, concerned about the potential disruption and crowding. Others believe that rezoning open park areas may be necessary due to rising land values in the area. The president of the Cronulla Chamber of Commerce, Mark Aprilovic, is skeptical about the feasibility of the proposal, raising questions about where the campers would be accommodated without offending local residents.

Jordan Henderson, a Liverpool midfielder, has signed a new five-year contract worth £100,000-a-week, keeping him at Anfield until 2020. Henderson, who joined Liverpool in 2011 for £16million, was determined to prove himself after being linked with a move to Fulham in 2012. He has had a strong season and is expected to take over the captaincy from Steven Gerrard. Henderson expressed his desire to stay at Liverpool long-term, having gone through difficult times but believing in the club's potential to win trophies. Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers hopes other players, including Raheem Sterling, Jordon Ibe, and Martin Skrtel, will follow Henderson's lead and sign new deals. Rodgers praised Henderson's development and the club's commitment to developing young players.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, has admitted trying to buy the toxin abrin, which is 30 times more deadly than ricin, from the dark web. The dark web is a subsection of the deep web, used for sharing information and trading goods anonymously and encrypted, and has attracted illegal activity such as selling drugs, pornographic content, and hacked information. The teenager was caught after expressing an interest in acquiring the toxin during online chats with undercover police. He showed awareness of the toxin's toxicity and potential harm. The investigation led to the arrest of the teenager and a 16-year-old girl, but she was later released without charge. In a previous case, a graphic designer named Kuntal Patel was the first person to be prosecuted under the Biological Weapons Act after she attempted to poison her mother on the dark web.

A family in Georgia can now legally use marijuana extract to treat their 5-year-old daughter's severe epilepsy, after Governor Nathan Deal signed a bill on Thursday. The bill, known as Haleigh's Hope Act, allows the use of low-THC cannabis oil for certain medical conditions, creating a registration process and research program. The Cox family had moved to Colorado in 2014, where medical marijuana is legal, after their daughter, Haleigh, was diagnosed with medication-resistant epilepsy and was having hundreds of seizures a day. The family had heard that cannabis oil might help, but it wasn't available in Georgia. Deal's signing of the bill will enable families to receive in-state treatment and return home. The law will benefit those with specific medical conditions, such as acute seizures. While medical marijuana is legal in nearly half the states, it remains illegal under federal law, creating a challenge for research and medical use.

Historian David Starkey made controversial remarks in an interview with the Daily Telegraph, attacking the "victim status" of ethnic minorities, disabled people, and women. He criticized Baroness Doreen Lawrence for treating black people as victims and claimed that all forms of liberation require individuals to refuse being victims. Starkey also denied being sexist but asserted that women tend to be of average intelligence, while men are either very bright or very thick. He criticized the current political class for lacking talent and being unable to be prime minister. Starkey, who was born with disabilities, also criticized the portrayal of disabled people as victims and claimed that fears of Islamophobia were victimizing Muslims.

Barcelona forward Pedro is considering his future at Camp Nou and could join Liverpool if Raheem Sterling leaves Anfield. Pedro, who has been linked with Liverpool before, would command £90,000-a-week wages, which is £10,000 less than Liverpool offered Sterling. Pedro is also less expensive than Sterling, who is valued at £50million. Barcelona's Pedro could become a realistic target for Liverpool if Sterling leaves. Pedro has been benched frequently this season due to Barcelona's all-star attack of Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez. He has also been linked with Inter Milan and Bayern Munich but may prefer Liverpool due to the wages and the opportunity to start regularly. Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers has scouted Pedro and could make a move for him. Barcelona cannot sign players until January 2016 but they may sell players like Alex Song if the price is right. Xavi Hernandez and Dani Alves are two players Barcelona want to keep but have not been able to agree on new contracts with them yet. Xavi is considering a move to Qatar, while Alves has offers from several big European clubs but has not ruled out staying at Barcelona.

Newcastle United fans are planning to boycott the club's next home game against Tottenham on April 19 in protest against owner Mike Ashley. A social media campaign has been launched to encourage fans to stay away from St James' Park and ensure the lowest ever Premier League crowd. A website, Sack Ashley.com, has been set up to promote the boycott and a visual and audible protest will take place before and after the game. Newcastle boss John Carver suffered a fourth successive defeat at Sunderland on Sunday, and the boycott and protests have also received the support of the Newcastle United Supporters Trust. The trust believes in supporter representation and ownership, and while it is not leading the campaign, it supports action that could lead to increased supporter representation or ownership.

Demi Moore is selling her Manhattan penthouse, which she once shared with ex-husband Bruce Willis, for a record-breaking $75 million. The 14-bedroom apartment, located in the historic San Remo building on the Upper West Side, includes 7,000 square feet of living space and wrap-around terraces with views of Central Park and the Hudson River. The couple purchased the penthouse and a two-bedroom maisonette in 1990 and decorated it in a Southwestern mission motif. The apartment features a 24 by 17 foot dining room, a living room with windows overlooking Central Park, and state-of-the-art kitchen appliances. Moore and Willis were married from 1987 until 2000 and have three daughters together. The combined monthly maintenance fees for both residences are over $20,000. The San Remo, designed in 1929 by American architect Emery Roth, is home to several famous neighbors, including Dustin Hoffman, Diane Keaton, Steven Spielberg, and U2 frontman Bono. Moore is selling the apartment and maisonette because she doesn't spend much time there anymore. The sale would break the record for the most expensive co-op apartment ever sold on the Upper West Side.

McDonald's announced plans to increase starting wages for full- and part-time employees at its company-owned restaurants in the US to a dollar above the minimum wage, starting July 1. The average wage is expected to be over $10 an hour by the end of 2016. McDonald's USA owns about 10% of the restaurants in the country, with the rest operated as franchises that will not be affected by the pay increases. The burger chain joins other corporations in raising wages against a backdrop of an improving economy and public pressure. McDonald's workers have staged protests in the past, demanding wages of $15 an hour and a union. The company has faced allegations of labor violations, including denial of overtime pay and unsafe working conditions. McDonald's USA President Mike Andres claimed the demonstrations did not affect the company's reputation. In addition to wage increases, McDonald's will offer paid time off for employees who have worked for the company for a year and work an average of 20 hours a week. McDonald's US business has been struggling, with sales and customer counts at established locations falling for two years in a row. The company named Steve Easterbrook as its new CEO in January, and the change took effect last month. McDonald's also plans to expand benefits to help workers complete high school and college.

Over 1,700 Chinese high school students in Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took their exams in the playground on Saturday due to insufficient indoor space. The students, particularly the freshmen, organized the outdoor exam themselves and even suggested it to broaden their horizons and prevent cheating. The school approved the proposal, and to avoid sun dazzle, regular radio announcements instructed students to turn their chairs and desks. The students believed this novel approach would encourage relaxation and test their organizing skills.

Inter Milan have initiated talks with Manchester City over a potential deal for forward Stevan Jovetic. Inter are proposing an initial loan deal, but City are reluctant to let him go on a temporary basis. Jovetic is expected to leave Manchester City this summer after being excluded from their Champions League squad to make way for Wilfried Bony. Inter's boss Roberto Mancini is keen on signing his former player, but City will only consider offers that recoup a significant portion of the £22million they paid Fiorentina for him in 2013. Inter are also considering a deal for Yaya Toure, who could be one of several players to leave Manchester City this summer. Toure has expressed a desire to play in Italy, and Mancini has expressed interest in bringing him to Inter. However, it will not be easy to sign Toure, as he is a player with great technique and character. Inter are unlikely to make Lukas Podolski's loan move from Arsenal permanent, leaving them in need of a wide forward.

A 30-year-old man named Patrick James Fredricksen, who is a known child sex offender, has been arrested in Utah for stealing a school bus and attempting to kidnap children. The incident occurred while Fredricksen was working at a baseball complex, where he allegedly stole master keys and later stole a funeral-parlor worker's car. He then used the keys to steal a school bus and attempted to pick up children from their homes using the bus's on-board list of children's names and addresses. Fredricksen was stopped by a sheriff's lieutenant after a report of a suspicious person driving a school bus. He is currently in jail for investigation of theft of a vehicle, attempted child kidnapping, and damaging a prison. Fredricksen has a history of criminal offenses, including unlawful sexual activity with a minor, impersonating a firefighter, and sexual exploitation of a minor. He is on Utah's Sex Offender Registry.

Former U.S. Marine Charlie Linville, who lost his right leg and several fingers in an explosion in Afghanistan, is making a second attempt to climb Mount Everest to inspire others with disabilities. He was stopped last year due to an avalanche that killed 16 Sherpa guides. Linville, who is using a specially designed metal foot with a climbing boot and crampons, plans to approach from the northern, Tibetan side with the Heroes Project team. He retired from the military and has been climbing with the nonprofit organization since. Linville, who is determined to overcome his challenges, said, "My message is anything is possible."

Liana Barrientos, a 39-year-old woman from New York, is facing criminal charges for falsifying marriage license applications during a period when she was married 10 times between 1999 and 2010. Prosecutors believe the marriages were part of an immigration scam, as some of her husbands filed for permanent residence status shortly after the weddings. Barrientos, who is currently married to four men, is charged with offering a false instrument for filing in the first degree and faces up to four years in prison if convicted. The case was referred to the Bronx District Attorney's Office by Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Department of Homeland Security's Investigation Division. Seven of her husbands are from "red-flagged" countries, and one was deported to Pakistan in 2006. Barrientos was arrested on additional charges of theft of service and criminal trespass after leaving court on Friday.

Mauricio Pochettino, the manager of Tottenham Hotspur, believes Harry Kane should win the PFA Player of the Year award over Eden Hazard of Chelsea. Pochettino praised Kane's impact on English football and his potential to become the first Spurs player to score 30 goals in a season since Gary Lineker. Kane has been nominated for the award, along with Hazard, Diego Costa (Chelsea), Alexis Sanchez (Arsenal), David de Gea (Manchester United), and Philippe Coutinho (Liverpool). Pochettino also defended Spurs' decision to play a one-off pre-season game against the MLS All-Stars in Colorado, stating that it was only one game and a good opportunity for a prestigious test.

A 66-year-old man from Palm Beach in Brisbane was arrested and charged with a 'breach of the peace' and public nuisance after allegedly burning an Australian flag at the Shrine of Remembrance in Anzac Square on Friday afternoon. The incident occurred on the eve of Anzac Day commemoration services, where tens of thousands of people are expected to gather around the Eternal Flame of Remembrance to pay their respects to fallen service men and women. The burning of the Australian flag has been condemned by the Returned and Services League (RSL) as "disgusting" and "not on." The man will face Brisbane Magistrate's Court on Saturday morning. The Anzac Day commemorations will begin with dawn services at 4.28am at the Shrine of Remembrance, and big screens will be set up around Anzac Square and other nearby locations to accommodate the large crowds.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is expressing the need for his team to make significant signings in the summer transfer window to keep up with their rivals. City were limited in their spending last summer due to UEFA's Financial Fair Play regulations, resulting in a net spending cap of £49 million. Pellegrini has identified the need to bring in a "crack" player, such as Sergio Aguero, to strengthen the squad. Despite the team's current fourth place standing in the Premier League, Pellegrini still believes they have a chance to retain the title. He is focusing on finishing the season strongly and has not yet discussed plans for next season. Pellegrini's comments could be perceived as a plea for more financial resources, but he has not explicitly stated whether a spending spree will be sanctioned. His immediate concern is securing a high league position.

Richard Sherman, a cornerback for the Seattle Seahawks, was devastated after their loss in the Super Bowl to the New England Patriots. However, just four days after the game, he welcomed a son, Rayden, with his girlfriend Ashley Moss. Sherman has shared photos of his newborn son on Instagram, and despite the loss, he was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Year by the Kansas City Committee of 101. Sherman will undergo surgery to repair a torn ligament in his left elbow during the off-season but is expected to return to the field in August when the Seahawks take on the Denver Broncos in their first preseason game.

A 29-year-old man named Pankaj Saw died after falling three storeys from an apartment balcony in Macquarie Park while on the phone with his new wife in India. The incident occurred on Thursday night, and emergency services were called to the scene, but Saw died at the scene due to serious head and internal injuries. It is believed that the wooden railing gave way, causing Saw to fall to the concrete below. Saw was in Australia on a long-stay work visa and had been working in Sydney for some time as a systems support analyst for an IT firm. He had recently returned from India, where he got married. Howard Ryan, director of Housesafe, inspected pictures of the balcony's bracket and believed it was installed in a non-compliant and unsafe manner, which may have contributed to the collapse. Saw's colleagues and friends gathered at his apartment to mourn his loss, and his manager described him as a man full of life and energy. Police are investigating whether a structural fault played a role in the fatal fall and are hoping to speak to the person who helped Saw before paramedics arrived.

An autopsy report revealed that 17-year-old Justus Howell, who was fatally shot by police in Zion, Illinois on Saturday, was hit twice in the back. According to a police spokesman, officers responded to an "argument" and chased Justus down the street before opening fire. Witnesses reported hearing an officer admit to shooting the teenager, who had moved to the area from Wisconsin in February and aspired to be a surgeon. The police chief did not return calls for comment, and it is unknown if an officer has been suspended during the investigation. The toxicology results are pending. Justus' mother, LaToya Howell, told Fox News that her son was not a threat when he was running away from the police.

Robert Durst, a millionaire and suspect in multiple crimes including the murder of his friend Susan Berman in California, pleaded not guilty to a new federal charge of possessing a gun after a felony conviction in Louisiana on Tuesday. Durst, who is currently being held in a state prison due to concerns about his suicide risk, also faces state weapons charges and a murder charge in California. The hearing had an unusual moment when Durst asked who the prosecutor was. Durst's lawyers argue that his previous federal gun convictions in Pennsylvania do not apply to Louisiana law. The arrest in New Orleans is believed to have been timed to coincide with the final episode of HBO's "The Jinx," which aired the day before his arrest and featured Durst making incriminating statements off-camera. Durst's lawyers claim that the search of his hotel room was illegal and that the arrest was a deliberate attempt to coincide with the show's conclusion. Federal prosecutors are also discussing a separate matter regarding two FBI agents and a state trooper who failed to appear at a hearing last week.

Wigan Warriors secured their first away win of the Super League season with a 40-22 victory over struggling Wakefield Trinity. Joe Burgess scored a hat-trick for Wigan, who climbed above St Helens into second place. Wakefield gave debuts to Ben Kavanagh, Jordan Crowther, and Ian Kirke, but both Kirke and Danny Washbrook suffered injuries. Wakefield made a good start with a try from Matt Ryan, but Wigan took control with tries from Dom Crosby and Matty Smith. Burgess and Dom Manfredi added tries before halftime, but Wakefield fought back with tries from Daniel Smith and Pita Godinet. Burgess scored his second try after the break, but Godinet responded with a try for Chris Riley. Wigan extended their lead with a try from Lee Mossop and Burgess completed his hat-trick. Wigan looked set for a comfortable win, but Wakefield gave them a scare with injuries and a determined performance.

Josh Warrington admitted to feeling bored during his lopsided points victory against Dennis Tubieron in Leeds. The 24-year-old featherweight, who has been compared to Ricky Hatton due to his impressive fan base, easily outclassed the Filipino fighter, who was smaller and had previously boxed at bantamweight and lightweight. Warrington made a fast start and picked Tubieron off with punches, but failed to deliver the stoppage that had looked likely. Tubieron, who had a record of 19 wins from 24 fights, was content to fight on the back foot and was marked up in the second round. He briefly threatened in the third round but Warrington finished the stronger. The fight was interrupted by a beach ball thrown from the crowd and the timekeeper stopped the action almost 60 seconds early. Warrington was awarded a landslide victory by the judges, but some critics have questioned his power and ability to deliver a stoppage at the top level. Warrington picked up the vacant WBC International title and is aiming for a world title shot within the next 12 months.

A nine-year-old boy named Tate Ricks went missing in the St. Johns River in Florida after the boat he was in with his grandmother's boyfriend capsized. The incident occurred when their 14-foot johnboat was hit by a wake from a larger boat around 5:30 pm on Saturday. The boy was not wearing a life jacket and both he and the man went into the water. The man was able to make it to shore but could not locate Tate. Authorities began a rescue operation on Saturday evening and are using sonar, thermal imaging, and divers to search the area. The search includes the St. Johns River from US-17 to Memorial Bridge to the north and Pico Road to the south. The Wildlife Conservation Commission is leading the investigation and the Putnam County Sheriff's Office is leading the search. The incident is being investigated as a boating accident and no foul play is suspected. Tate is a third-grade student at Kelly Smith Elementary School in Palatka and is described as a fun-loving kid who enjoys hunting, fishing, and NASCAR. His family is staying positive and asking for prayers. The search is ongoing and crews will remain on the river all night and through the weekend.

An Albuquerque man, identified as Sergio Barrientos-Hinojosa, argued with a customer at a gas station and opened fire, using his 13-year-old son as a getaway driver. No one was injured in the incident, which occurred while police were holding a DUI checkpoint on the other side of the road. Barrientos-Hinojosa reportedly fired several gunshots during the escape, and his son was left "shell-shocked" by the experience. Police later pulled over the car and found the gun that was used in the shooting. Barrientos-Hinojosa is facing charges including child abuse, but it is unclear if he has an attorney. The incident began when Barrientos-Hinojosa asked his son to take him to buy beer at the gas station, where an argument ensued and led to the shooting.

Kevin Carr, a 34-year-old athlete from Woolacombe, Devon, has set a new record as the fastest man to run around the world, completing the 16,300-mile journey in 621 days. Carr ran more than a marathon a day every day for almost two years, crossing 26 countries and getting through 16 pairs of shoes. He faced numerous challenges during his journey, including attacks by bears and wild dogs, being run over twice, and extreme weather conditions. Carr was also the first man to complete the run unsupported, pushing all of his equipment in a stroller that weighed twice as much as he does. The highlight of his journey was running through the Andes mountains, but he also encountered dangerous wildlife and traffic in various countries. Carr's trip took him through Europe, India, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, and the US, and he lost three stone during the trip. He used bear bangers and relied on people with short-distance radios to keep him safe during stretches with bears and wolves. Carr's journey took him to various locations around the world, from Alabama to Chile. He faced indifference from some people and endured severe heatstroke and being hit by cars during his journey.

A Georgia middle school teacher, Nancy Perry, has been removed from the classroom and will retire at the end of the year after she expressed her critical personal opinions about President Barack Obama to students. Perry is accused of telling students that Obama is a Muslim and that any parent who supports him couldn't be Christian. A 12-year-old student brought the matter to his father, Jimmie Scott, who complained to the school. During a parent-teacher conference, Perry and her husband showed Scott anti-Obama internet propaganda. Superintendent Chuck Ledbetter apologized to the student and his parents and stated that teachers should not attempt to persuade students about religious or political beliefs in the classroom. Perry's husband, who sits on the county Board of Education, should not have attended the parent-teacher conference, and school principals are now required to call the superintendent if any board member requests to sit in on such meetings. Scott also addressed the community at the meeting, expressing that his family had been ridiculed and had racial slurs thrown at them. Scott is black, and Perry is white.

Sunderland footballer Adam Johnson, 27, has been charged with four offenses including grooming and sexual activity with a 15-year-old girl. The charges were made under the Sexual Offenses Act 2003. Johnson, who is Sunderland's top scorer, was suspended by the club after his arrest in March but was later allowed to train and play as a substitute. Following the charges, Sunderland's chiefs are under pressure to suspend Johnson again, which would mean he would miss the remaining six games for the team. The club is just above the Premier League drop zone and has a match against Stoke tomorrow. Johnson is due to appear at Peterlee Magistrates Court on May 20. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has urged the public not to share any information online that could prejudice the proceedings, and the complainant is entitled to lifelong anonymity under the law.

A 35-year-old man named James Webster was spared jail time after admitting to outraging public decency by filming up women's skirts at a Lidl store in Maidenhead, Berkshire. Webster used a hidden camera with a hole cut in a bag to carry out his covert filming as women bent over freezers. He was caught by a fellow shopper who noticed his suspicious behavior and reported it to security guards. Webster initially denied any wrongdoing but later turned himself in to the police. He expressed remorse for his actions and was struggling with a break-up at the time. The court heard that Webster had no prior convictions and had been smoking cannabis around the time of the incident but was now clean. He was sentenced to a three-year community order and ordered to take part in a sexual offences treatment programme. He was also fined £60 and ordered to pay £85 in costs.

A New Zealand man, Matthew Bird, drastically reduced his income by quitting his high-paying job as an agricultural adviser to become a mechanic in order to avoid a significant increase in his child support payments. Bird was previously expected to pay $1,300 a month, but after Inland Revenue amended their child support formula in April, his payment rose to $1,900 a month. Bird stated that this increase was "unreasonable" and believed that illegal employment would become more prevalent under the new system. Another man, Dean Sorenson, also faced financial difficulties due to an increase in his child support payments by $172 a month. While Sorenson considered changing jobs to reduce his payment, he believed his family would suffer if he did. New Zealand MP Jo Goodhew invited parents struggling with the new formula to discuss how it was affecting their wages in her office. Inland Revenue advised parents to check the information they provided to ensure their payments were calculated correctly. Two offices reported dealing with a total of eight cases related to child support payment changes in 2015, but none were related to the recent amendments.

Newcastle United manager John Carver called Moussa Sissoko's red card tackle on Liverpool's Lucas "indefensible" after their 2-0 defeat at Anfield. Sissoko was sent off for two yellow cards, but Carver believed a straight red could have been given for the tackle. Carver also expressed frustration over a penalty call not given to Ayoze Perez. Despite the loss, which was Newcastle's fifth in a row, Carver saw some positives in his team's performance and felt they held their own against Liverpool. Sissoko could face disciplinary action for his tackle.

Manchester City is currently leading the Premier League with a four-point advantage over Liverpool, but the team's poor form in recent matches has raised concerns about their ability to maintain their position. With high-profile players like Yaya Toure and Samir Nasri set to leave in the summer, City faces challenges in identifying suitable replacements. The team's recent signings, such as Eliaquim Mangala and Stevan Jovetic, have failed to live up to expectations. Manchester City's long-term plan is to bring in Pep Guardiola as manager, but if they fail to secure the Premier League title this season, their financial capacity to rebuild the team may be limited due to the absence of Champions League money. The team's performance this season under Manuel Pellegrini has been weak, and keeping him on for another year while waiting for Guardiola to join is a significant gamble. City's capacity to improve would be severely limited if they are unable to secure a Champions League spot, and it is unclear whether Guardiola would be interested in joining under those circumstances.

The article reports on the surge in sales of Manny Pacquiao's boxing gear and merchandise ahead of his May 2 megafight against Floyd Mayweather. Philippine retailers, both online and in stores, are experiencing a significant increase in demand from fans looking to buy items such as T-shirts, boxing gloves, figurines, caps, and jackets. Prices for Pacquiao-autographed items have risen sharply, with buyers hoping to make a profit if he wins the fight. Pacquiao's own store, Team Pacquiao, has seen sales nearly triple, and even street vendors are making a profit selling lower-priced Pacquiao T-shirts. Pacquiao is widely regarded as a national idol in the Philippines, and thousands of fans are expected to watch free screenings of the fight in Manila. Despite being seen as the underdog, Pacquiao's followers are confident he will win the fight.

Novak Djokovic, the world's top-ranked tennis player, apologized to a ball boy who was caught in the middle of an angry outburst towards his support team during the Miami Open final against Andy Murray. Djokovic lost his cool after losing the second set and grabbed a towel from the startled ball boy during the heated exchange. Umpire Damien Dumusois gave Djokovic a code violation for the outburst. In a video posted on Facebook, Djokovic expressed his regret and apologized to the ball boy and his parents. He acknowledged that as a father, he wouldn't want his son to experience such a situation. Djokovic also mentioned that the emotions got the better of him during the intense match, but he learned to control them as a professional athlete. Despite the incident, Djokovic went on to win the third set 6-0 and claimed his fifth Miami Open title.

The upcoming Floyd Mayweather vs. Manny Pacquiao boxing match in Las Vegas is anticipated to generate around $400m in revenue. The referee for the highly-anticipated bout will earn $10,000. Kenny Bayless and Tony Weeks are considered front-runners for the role, with Bayless having previously refereed one of Mayweather's fights. Both fighters are in their final stages of preparation, with Mayweather revealing he is close to the welterweight limit, and Pacquiao showcasing his skills during a training session in Los Angeles. Pacquiao's trainer Freddie Roach has requested a fair referee for the contest, assuring that the best man will win.

Roma ended their four-month winless streak at home in the Serie A match against Napoli with a 1-0 victory. Miralem Pjanic scored the only goal in the 25th minute after a swift counter-attack. Goalkeeper Morgan de Sanctis was excellent in the second half, saving several shots by Napoli. Roma moved provisionally four points ahead of city rivals Lazio, while Napoli's winless streak was extended to five matches. Security was tight for Napoli's first visit to Roma since a fan of the southern club died following a shooting before last season's Italian Cup final. Roma was without injured captain Francesco Totti and fellow forward Gervinho, but Pjanic made an impact with a free kick and a goal. Napoli may have had a case for a penalty, but there was little protest. In the second half, de Sanctis made several saves to protect the three points. Napoli forward Lorenzo Insigne came on late for his first action since tearing his knee in November.

The parents of Martin Richard, the youngest victim of the Boston Marathon bombings in 2013, have made an emotional plea to the Justice Department to remove the death penalty from the table for Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who was convicted last week on all charges related to the bombings. The Richards wrote in a front-page opinion piece in The Boston Globe about the toll the trial and evidence have taken on their family, particularly the death of their 8-year-old son and the injuries to their 7-year-old daughter. They understand the heinousness of the crimes but urge the government to bring the case to a close by taking the death penalty off the table and sentencing Tsarnaev to life in prison without parole and waiving all appeals. They believe this would end the anguish and allow their family and the city of Boston to move forward. The sentencing phase of the trial is expected to begin on Tuesday and could last for four weeks.

According to a study by YouGov, people named Nigel are twice as likely to vote for the UK Independence Party (Ukip) compared to the general population. The research also found that Charlotte, Fiona, and Pauline are the names most likely to vote Conservative, while Sharon, Samantha, and Clare are least likely. Michelle, June, and Andy are the names most likely to vote Labour, and Nigel, Nick, and Jonathan are the least likely. Tim, Kathryn, and Samantha are the most likely names to vote for the Liberal Democrats. The study comes after a Ukip election candidate, Kim Rose, was investigated by the police for providing sausage rolls at an event, which could be considered a criminal offense known as "treating." Rose denies any wrongdoing and believes voters are unlikely to change their minds for a sausage roll.

A headteacher, David Nicholson, from The Costello School in Basingstoke, Hampshire, has resigned after allegations surfaced that he used his school email to arrange a threesome with a prostitute while she was dressed as a schoolgirl. The married father-of-four reportedly sent explicit messages to the escort, expressing his desire for her to dress up and be spanked. The meeting was supposed to take place in a hotel room while Nicholson was away from home. The investigation by Ofsted is ongoing. Nicholson, who previously worked as a headteacher in Chippenham, Wiltshire, and is training to be an Ofsted inspector, started at The Costello School last September. There are no concerns regarding pupil safeguarding, and the board has accepted his resignation. The school's chair of governors, Carol Bode, confirmed that business as usual would continue, with Mr Leigh Adams acting as headteacher.

An 83-year-old man named Thomas Cain was surprised with a long-lost photograph of his mother, Ora Mae, whom he had assumed had no photographic record. His granddaughter, Andrea Ferrell, found the image from a distant relative in Florida after a two-year search. The moment of discovery is captured in a video where Thomas Cain is shown in shock and tears upon realizing the photograph is of his mother. The family was thrilled to give him this unexpected gift. Thomas Cain's mother died in 1943 when he was just 13 years old. The photograph dates back to the 1920s and shows Ora Mae as a teenager. Andrea Ferrell described her grandfather as the "greatest, most humble, God-fearing, family-oriented, loving man in the entire world" and is also on a quest to find photographs of other ancestors, including Thomas Cain's father, Henry.

A new app called Honest has been launched, allowing users to ask personal questions anonymously and receive feedback from other anonymous users. Questions range from relationship dilemmas to sexual dysfunction and career changes. The creators, London advertising executives Ed and Rob Watts, aim to provide unbiased opinions and advice from a global society, using the concept of "collective intelligence." Users have asked questions such as "My long-term girlfriend is bad in bed, shall I tell her?" and "Shall I tell my girlfriend I hired a prostitute?" Responses vary, and the app can be downloaded for free on iOS.

On opening day at Wrigley Field, Chicago Cubs fans endured long waits to use the bathroom, with some resorting to using plastic cups due to the extensive lines. The bathroom issue caused fans to miss innings and uploaded pictures of the queues and plastic cups filled with urine on social media. The Cubs and Wrigley Field attributed the problem to two bathrooms on the upper deck going down temporarily, exacerbating existing wait time issues. Fans expressed their frustration on social media, with some missing innings and others reporting that toilets wouldn't flush. The Cubs apologized for the inconvenience and plan to add portable bathrooms and monitor wait times to address the issue moving forward.

A study conducted by The Tab, a student newspaper, found that students enrolled in computer science and dentistry courses at British universities are less likely to have had sex. Eleven percent of computer science students and nine percent of physicists reported being virgins. In contrast, students in Arts subjects like history and English were more likely to have had sex, with just one percent of students in these fields reporting that they were virgins. The average number of sexual partners for university students in Britain is 8.2. The survey also revealed that 22 percent of students didn't lose their virginity until they were 18, while 19 percent lost it at 16 and 15 percent lost it at 17. A shocking 1.66 percent of students reported losing their virginity when they were 13 or younger. The universities where students lost their virginity earliest included Aston and Ulster, with seven percent of students reporting that they had done so. On the other hand, ten percent of students from Lancaster University and nine percent from Kent and Royal Holloway University reported that they were still virgins.

Sam Allardyce, the manager of West Ham United, is making preparations for the upcoming season, but his future with the club is uncertain as his contract expires at the end of the current season. West Ham's co-owners, David Gold and David Sullivan, have scheduled a meeting with Allardyce at the end of May to discuss his position. Allardyce is focusing on the upcoming games and has begun planning for next season, but he is unsure if he will still be the manager. West Ham currently sits on 42 points in the Premier League, seven games before the end of the season.

A giraffe named Katie at the Dallas Zoo gave birth to a new calf in a live streamed event by Animal Planet. The labor lasted for over an hour and was captured by 10 cameras. The gender and condition of the newborn were not immediately known, but signs of life such as moving ears, standing efforts, and nursing were observed. Katie, described as a "diva" among the herd, held up well during the event with her long tongue sticking out on cue. The newborn joins a 4-year-old sister, Jamie. The exact number of online viewers was not mentioned, but fellow giraffes, including Katie's friend Jade, were present to witness the birth. Katie's gestation period was 15 months on average.

A new Aldi store in Avlaston, Derbyshire, attracted long queues of eager customers who waited up to 10 hours overnight for the chance to win prizes and get their hands on deals. The first 100 people through the door received golden tickets, with prizes including a 21.5inch television. Ivy and Brian Bacon, who traveled from Basford in Nottingham, were the lucky winners of the top prize. The store, which will create 29 jobs and have a car park, was officially opened by former Derby County player and BBC radio commentator Craig Ramage. Aldi made a £250 donation to the local council and donated children's treats and baby products to Alvaston Children's Centre. The store is one of 60 Aldi stores opening across the UK this year.

A 20-year-old woman identified as Britney E. Montenegro was arrested in Orlando, Florida, after getting involved in a fight involving 'multiple individuals' in the early hours of Saturday. The incident started inside a bar and spilled out onto the streets at East Pine Street and South Court Avenue around 2.40 am. Montenegro, who is originally from Queens, New York, and attends Valencia Community College, was covered in blood but it was not her own. She allegedly tried to attack another woman during the fight and was charged with disorderly conduct. Montenegro had a minor injury on her shoulder but was unable to explain how she sustained it. The police report noted that she also had another person's blood on her.

Everton manager Roberto Martinez defended Ross Barkley's decision to take a penalty against Burnley instead of Leighton Baines, despite Baines having a successful record from the spot. Barkley's effort was saved, but Everton went on to win 1-0 with a goal from Kevin Mirallas. Martinez argued that he trusts multiple players to take penalties and that Barkley showed responsibility in taking the shot. Baines has scored 15 penalties from 16 attempts in the Premier League for Everton.

Chef Ally Lees from Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a giant omelette for Easter, which contains 12,000 calories and 945g of protein. The omelette, which is three-foot in circumference and took an hour to cook, is recommended for a group of no fewer than five people to share. The dish, made using 150 eggs, is almost five times the daily intake for a grown man and the biggest omelette Chef Ally has ever cooked.

Jackie Stewart, a three-time Formula One world champion, has expressed concern over the disappearance of traditional European races from the Formula One calendar, specifically the German Grand Prix. The German GP was removed from the 2015 schedule due to financial issues, and the Italian Grand Prix is also in doubt. F1 races have been moving towards lucrative venues in Asia and the Middle East. Stewart believes that essential races in Germany, Italy, Britain, France, and Monaco should be preserved as they contributed significantly to the growth of motorsport. The German Grand Prix's absence means the 2015 season will consist of 19 races. Bernie Ecclestone, F1 supremo, has not been able to guarantee the future of the Italian Grand Prix.

A middle school teacher, Catherine Engelhardt, was assaulted by a student's mother, Annika McKenzie, and McKenzie's 14-year-old niece at Alverta B. Gray Schultz Middle School in Hempstead, New York. The incident occurred on Wednesday afternoon when McKenzie, without being cleared by security, waited for Engelhardt in the hallway and attacked her because she believed the teacher had "put her hands" on her 12-year-old daughter. Engelhardt was shoved against the wall, placed in a headlock, and thrown to the floor. Several students also became involved in the attack. Engelhardt was unconscious for several minutes and was rushed to the hospital. She has since been released and is recovering at home. McKenzie and her niece were arrested at the scene and charged with second-degree assault on school grounds, a felony, and second-degree strangulation. Engelhardt had previously expressed concerns about her safety at the school due to the lack of respect the students showed towards adults. The attack was caught on the school's security cameras.

A 24-year-old man named Mohamad Saeed Kodaimati from San Diego was arrested and charged with lying to federal agents about his involvement with Islamic State militants in Syria. Saeed, a Syrian national who became a naturalized American citizen in 2008, is accused of making false statements during interviews with the FBI and other US authorities at the US Embassy in Ankara, Turkey, in March. The Justice Department stated that Saeed falsely claimed he had not been involved in any fighting, had never fired his weapon at anyone, and did not know any Islamic State members. However, evidence gathered during the investigation, including Facebook photos and posts, contradicts these statements. Saeed allegedly bragged about working for a sharia court, openly expressed his support for ISIS, and claimed he had fought in a gun battle that lasted four months. Saeed traveled from San Diego to Istanbul and was in Syria and Turkey until his return to the United States in March. He was arrested in Rancho Bernardo, San Diego, and made his initial court appearance on Thursday, where he was ordered held without bail.

Sheffield Wednesday secured a 1-0 win against Brentford in the Championship, with Kieran Lee scoring the only goal in the second half. Both teams played with high defensive lines, resulting in numerous long balls but few finding their mark. The first half produced few chances, with Caolan Lavery coming closest for Wednesday. The second half saw more action, with Andre Gray having a good opportunity for Brentford, but both teams struggled to create clear-cut scoring opportunities. Harlee Dean made a costly mistake, but Wednesday failed to capitalize. The breakthrough came in the 75th minute when Lee scored from close range after a parried ball. Brentford had chances to equalize, but missed them, including Alan Judge blasting over the goal from a one-on-one situation. Another mistake from Dean almost led to a second goal for Wednesday, but Bus' shot was off target.

A man named Carlos Colina, 32, is currently in custody after being accused of chopping up his friend's body and disposing of it in an apartment building's recycling bin in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
