Colina had previously been involved in a violent altercation at the Cambridge Athletic Club, where he was a member. Witnesses reported that Colina had punched a smaller man repeatedly during a dispute over gym equipment, leaving the victim with bloody cuts and broken ribs. Colina was subsequently kicked out of the gym and has an outstanding assault and battery case pending against him. The victim of the altercation, Jonathan Camilien, 26, was later found dead with his remains discovered in a duffel bag near the Massachusetts Institute of Technology campus and his head found in Colina's apartment building. Colina is believed to have known Camilien, as they were friends on Facebook and had lived together in Somerville. The Middlesex District Attorney has classified Camilien's death as a homicide, but no motive has been released. Colina is currently being held on $1 million bail and is scheduled for a pretrial hearing on April 14. Police found a saw, rope, and cleaning supplies in Colina's apartment.

Maurizio Arrivabene, the team principal of Ferrari, has urged Kimi Raikkonen to improve his performances if he wants to continue driving for the Maranello marque beyond the current Formula One season. Raikkonen's contract expires at the end of the year, with an option for 2016 if both parties agree. The Finn has expressed his happiness working with the team, but his form has not been as strong as teammate Sebastian Vettel's. Raikkonen has struggled in qualifying, but has recovered well in the last two races to finish fourth in Malaysia and China. Arrivabene has stated that results need to improve for Raikkonen to remain with the team. Raikkonen has shown his speed and appears keen on staying, but Arrivabene has made it clear that performance is the key factor.

A New Zealand hunter, Max Verschuuren, survived being mistaken for a deer and shot in the back by his friend during a hunting trip in the Te Urewera forest, North Island. Verschuuren was bent over emptying rocks out of his boot when his friend mistook the reflection of his dim headlight for a deer's eyes and fired a .270 rifle. Verschuuren tumbled down the hill and called out to his friends, who then realized their mistake. The shooter was remorseful and visited Verschuuren every day in the hospital. Verschuuren received stitches and was expected to be discharged later on Monday. Local police are investigating the incident and issued a warning to hunters to take appropriate safety measures. Verschuuren, a keen hunter, plans to continue shooting despite the incident.

A family in Washington reportedly had their three-year-old's baby monitor hacked, resulting in a stranger's voice coming through the device and potentially accessing the camera feed. The parents had initially dismissed their son's complaints of someone talking to him at night as an overactive imagination. However, one night they heard the hacker say, "Wake up little boy, daddy's looking for you." The family believes the hacker had control over both the audio and camera functions of the monitor. After the incident, they reported it to Foscam, the company where they bought the device, but have not received a definitive answer on the origin of the hack. Technology experts have warned that as more baby monitors connect to the internet, they become easier targets for hackers. Parents are advised to change the passwords on their devices to make them more secure. Another family from Minnesota recently experienced a similar issue, with their baby monitor and camera footage being accessed and shared online.

New York Mayor Bill de Blasio, who served as campaign manager for Hillary Clinton's successful 2000 Senate run, has not endorsed her in her current presidential campaign and wants to see a clear vision from her on addressing income inequality before doing so. De Blasio believes Clinton's campaign message needs to be defined and emphasizes the importance of progressive taxation, increasing wages and benefits, and taxing the wealthy to invest in infrastructure and education. He also highlights Clinton's previous efforts to listen to everyday people and believes it will be crucial for her to do so again in light of the economic hardships caused by the Great Recession.

Angelique Kerber won the Family Circle Cup on Sunday, defeating Madison Keys in a thrilling three-set match. Kerber rallied from behind to win six of the last seven games, including the final game where Keys made four straight errors. Kerber broke serve five times in the match, while Keys, who hadn't lost serve all week, finished with 57 unforced errors. In the semifinals, Kerber defeated countrywoman and defending champion Andrea Petkovic. Keys had dominated her opponents leading up to the final but struggled to keep up with Kerber's consistency and relentless play. The German won 83% of her first serves and broke serve three times in the first set. Keys had won their only previous meeting in three sets at Eastbourne last June.

A bearded dragon named Liz, owned by Shannen Hussein, has gained attention for seemingly understanding the English language. In a video taken during mealtime, Liz nods her head in response to Shannen asking if she's hungry. The reptile is rewarded with a superworm treat for her conversational skills. Liz isn't the only unique pet on Shannen's hobby farm; her pet lamb Winter is also an online sensation. Other animals on the farm include cats, birds, a snake, and ducklings, as well as turtles, a llama, and what appears to be an emu. Liz is particularly fond of superworms and will do anything to get one.

Esteban Cambiasso, a midfielder for Leicester City and former Argentina international, has expressed that helping Leicester avoid relegation from the Premier League would be a significant achievement in his career. Cambiasso, who has previously won five Serie A titles and the Champions League with Inter Milan, views saving Leicester as equivalent to winning a trophy. Leicester, currently at the bottom of the Premier League table, will need to win a majority of their remaining matches to avoid relegation. Cambiasso, who joined Leicester last summer on a free transfer, is confident in the team's ability to turn their season around and stay in the league. Leicester faces West Ham United at home on Saturday. Cambiasso won five consecutive Serie A titles with Inter Milan between 2005 and 2010 and represented Argentina 52 times, scoring five goals.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers believes his team's recent defeats are due to their own mistakes and not because opponents have figured out their tactics. The Reds had an unbeaten run in the Premier League with their 3-4-2-1 formation but have struggled to create chances in their last few games, resulting in losses to Manchester United and Arsenal. Rodgers insists that the team's performances are to blame and not the opposition. Liverpool is now out of the Champions League qualification places and will look to the FA Cup as their only chance to save the season. They face Blackburn in the quarter-final replay on Wednesday, and Rodgers is focused on reaching the semi-finals in the cup competitions. Blackburn, who have eliminated top-flight sides Swansea and Stoke, will also be determined to reach Wembley and cause an upset against Liverpool.

The London Book Fair Author HQ is a three-day event offering seminars for new authors, featuring experts from publishing houses, agencies, and successful authors. Topics include publishing industry insights, digital publishing, and career launches. Genre Spotlights focus on crime/thrillers and contemporary fiction, and there's a seminar on legal issues and crowdfunding. The London Book and Screen Week runs simultaneously, offering various literary and film events across the city. The Fair is at Olympia, West London, and a three-day pass costs £35. Seminars are first-come, first-served.

Burton Albion manager Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink led his team to promotion to League One after a 2-1 win over Morecambe. However, Hasselbaink is not content with just promotion and wants to win the championship title as well. Burton Albion secured the promotion after Wycombe drew at Wimbledon. Hasselbaink praised his team's performance against Morecambe and also paid tribute to his predecessor Gary Rowett for laying the foundation for the team's success. The team will now focus on their next two games in League Two and aim to prepare well for the challenge in League One.

Japanese airline All Nippon Airways (ANA) is set to unveil a new Boeing 787 Dreamliner livery inspired by the Star Wars character R2-D2. The plane's cockpit and front half of the fuselage will be painted with blue panels in the shape of R2-D2's design. The rest of the plane will feature the Star Wars logo and ANA's regular blue livery on the tail. The new Star Wars: The Force Awakens teaser trailer was also released, showcasing X-Wing battles, the Millennium Falcon, and appearances by Han Solo, Chewbacca, and new cast members. Fans in the US and UK reacted positively to the trailer and the ANA livery news.

Josh Warrington, a featherweight boxer from Britain, will have Vinnie Jones accompany him into the ring during his fight in Leeds on Saturday. Warrington is gaining popularity and aims for a world title within the next year. The article also mentions other celebrities who have joined boxers in the ring for their walks. These include Justin Bieber and Lil Wayne with Floyd Mayweather, Liam Gallagher with Ricky Hatton, Prince Naseem Hamed with Puff Daddy, Nathan Cleverly with Mickey Rourke and Tom Jones, and Andrew Flintoff with Carl Frampton and Raul Hirales.

PayPal's top developer, Jonathan Leblanc, presented the idea of edible passwords during a presentation called 'Kill All Passwords.' The devices would be powered by stomach acid and include mini computers, eliminating the need for traditional passwords or biometric methods like fingerprint scanning. PayPal is exploring various physical methods for identity verification, such as edible capsules that check glucose levels or blood pressure, silicon chips under the skin, and wearable computer tattoos. However, PayPal later clarified that these ideas were not currently being developed by the company. The article also mentions True Key, an app that uses facial recognition instead of passwords for website logins. Passwords have long been criticized for their weaknesses, with common passwords like 'password' and '123456' being easily hacked. The average person struggles to remember the 19 passwords they need, making more secure and convenient methods a priority.

Gareth Bale suffered a calf strain after only two minutes in Real Madrid's league game against Malaga on Saturday, making it unlikely that he will play in the second leg of the Champions League against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday. Bale's injury occurred less than five minutes into the game and he was replaced by Marco Asensio. The Welsh forward had not been injured since October of last year, and his absence will be a significant blow to Real Madrid as they prepare for their most important game of the season. Cristiano Ronaldo was the first player to check on Bale after he went down injured, and Real Madrid went on to win the game 3-1. Bale's absence could mean that Carlo Ancelotti will continue with a four-man midfield and a front line of Ronaldo and Karim Benzema, who was also injured in the game against Malaga.

Swansea manager Garry Monk is determined to prevent his former boss Roberto Martinez from getting a win at the Liberty Stadium as Everton look to finish the season strongly after a tough campaign. Everton qualified for Europe last season but have struggled this term, with Martinez under pressure following a string of poor results. Swansea, on the other hand, have been impressive and Monk wants them to continue their form and surpass their previous best Premier League points total. The article mentions the impact of Europe on domestic performances and Swansea's point against Everton in November, where Martinez criticized Swansea's tactics. Monk insists there are no hard feelings and is focused on getting a win for Swansea.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar, who was drunk, jumped into the lions' enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. He shouted that he would "kill a lion" and surprised the security guards. Kumar ran towards the lions, shouting the same thing, but fell into a moat along the way. The guards were able to rescue him before he reached the animals. Kumar later explained that he was drunk and thought he could handle the lions. The police cautioned him and sent him for psychiatric evaluation. Last year, a 20-year-old man was killed by a tiger in Delhi after he climbed into its enclosure at the city zoo.

Joe Giudice, a star on the Real Housewives of New Jersey, had his driving license suspended for two years by a state judge due to his "worst ever seen" driving record. Giudice, who is preparing to go to federal prison for bankruptcy fraud, was fined $10,000, the maximum amount. He pleaded guilty to unlawful use of an ID and impersonation in October and received an 18-month sentence. His wife, Teresa, is also serving a 15-month federal sentence on the same charges. The judge called Giudice's disregard for the law into question, citing numerous previous driving infractions and suspensions. Despite his lawyer's argument that Giudice is destitute and unable to pay the fine, the judge refused after Giudice recently received $75,000 for prison photos and a tell-all interview. Giudice used his brother's identity to obtain a driver's license while his own was suspended for driving while intoxicated in 2010. The Giudices pleaded guilty to bankruptcy fraud in 2014 and were ordered to pay restitution of over $400,000. Giudice, who is an Italian citizen, is expected to be deported once his prison term ends.

The article introduces the greater adjutant stork, a majestic endangered bird that resides near the Boragaon landfill in Guwahati, India. The landfill, which covers 94 acres and is mostly made up of fresh waste, attracts the stork and photographer Timothy Bouldry. Bouldry has been traveling the world for the past seven years photographing landfills and became connected with the residents of Boragaon. Approximately 100 families live in the landfill, making a living by searching for valuable items and selling them. Despite the challenging conditions, which include no electricity or running water, the residents are content and expert at repurposing. Bouldry has found humanitarian photo projects to be the most fulfilling and has been living and working inside the La Chureca landfill in Nicaragua, helping the community grow gardens and teaching English and yoga classes. Bouldry is a photographer based in New Hampshire and can be followed on Facebook and Twitter.

American rapper Tyga visited Arsenal's Emirates Stadium and was given a red No. 52 Arsenal shirt by Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Kieran Gibbs. Tyga, who is currently touring in the UK, posed for pictures in the dressing room and even dyed his hair red to show his support for the team. Oxlade-Chamberlain could return to action for Arsenal's game against Hull, while Gibbs is competing for a starting spot at left back. Tyga has been making headlines for his relationship with Kylie Jenner, the youngest Kardashian sister.

The US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit has ruled that Asian-American rock band The Slants cannot trademark their name because it is considered disparaging to Asians. The band, which plays a type of grunge music called Chinatown Dance Rock, applied for trademarks in 2010 and 2011, but were rejected both times due to the disparaging nature of their name. The band's lawyer argued that the name was a healthy reappropriation of a term usually considered a slur, but the court found that there was evidence the term is offensive to people of Asian descent. The court also noted that a refusal to federally register a trademark does not prevent the applicant from using it. The case has parallels to the Washington Redskins' lawsuit against the US Patent and Trademark Office, which cancelled the NFL team's trademarks due to the name disparaging Native Americans. The team is currently appealing the decision. The court's decision was criticized by the band's lawyer as unnecessarily politicized, and the USPTO declined to comment. A judge in a separate opinion suggested that it might be time to revisit the federal trademark law's disparagement provisions.

Manchester City will face Crystal Palace and their top scorer Glenn Murray, who has scored a goal every 91 minutes in the Premier League this season, making him the deadliest striker statistically. Harry Kane and Diego Costa are currently tied for the top spot in goal scoring with 19 each, but Murray ranks higher due to his superior minutes-per-goal ratio. Other top scorers include Olivier Giroud, Papiss Cisse, and Chelsea's Diego Costa, who is expected to miss two weeks with a hamstring injury. Chelsea has four players in the top 10, including Andre Schurrle and Frank Lampard, who has a better ratio than Sergio Aguero. Murray, who has scored four goals in 364 minutes for Palace, has the best minutes-per-goal ratio of all.

A small business, Memories Gourmet Pizza Co., based in Wisconsin, faced backlash and unwanted attention when people mistook them for Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana, which made headlines for refusing to cater a same-sex wedding. The confusion led to angry comments and calls to protest, thrusting the Wisconsin business into the national debate over Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act. The owners, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke, were shocked and distressed by the situation, which began on April Fool's Day. They tried to clarify their identity on Facebook but also received support from some people. Premeau is concerned that the misinformation and defamation could harm their wholesale pizza business.

Exeter, a city in Devon, England, is facing the issue of being deemed "too posh" for the Old Kent Road spot in a planned Monopoly edition. Game makers have been unable to find a suitable low-rent area in Exeter to fill the brown section of the board, which is typically occupied by Old Kent Road and Whitechapel Road in the London version. Thousands of voters have suggested landmarks for the more expensive slots, but none have come forward for the lower end. Exeter, which has recently seen an influx of luxury student flats and high-end developments, has outdone other cities in getting its own Monopoly edition, but the lack of suggestions for the brown spots is unprecedented for game makers. Exeter City Council Leader Pete Edwards agrees that there is no suitable area for the brown spots and believes that whoever gets Old Kent Road will be criticized. The makers of the game have launched a second appeal for recommendations and have sent representatives to Exeter to find a location.

A New York teacher, Madeline Luciano, was fired after an incident where she allowed eighth grade students at PS 18 in Manhattan to write down negative words about a classmate on the blackboard. The words included "ugly," "annoying," and "phony." The exercise was intended to teach students to be kinder to each other, but it escalated into bullying with the girl crying. Luciano claims she tried to stop the bullying and disciplined the student writing the nasty comments. She has since been fired and is now suing the city's education department to get her license back to work in another school. The incident was not the first time the girl had been bullied, and her bookbag had been hidden that day. Luciano has worked for New York's education department since 2010.

Virginia Trimble Ritter, whose daughter Marcia was raped and murdered in 1975, recently requested and viewed crime scene photos of her daughter's body for the first time in over 40 years. Marcia's body was found 33 days after she disappeared, and Ritter's then-husband advised her against seeing the photos. Jerome Sydney Barrett was convicted of Marcia's murder in 2009, and Ritter now regrets not seeing the photos earlier. She described her daughter's appearance in the photos as unrecognizable due to injuries, but some parts of her body looked like Marcia. Marcia's body was found in a rarely used garage, and she had been strangled and sexually assaulted. The case went unsolved for 33 years until Barrett's arrest in 2006, after DNA on Marcia's clothing matched his. Barrett had been in prison on sex charges between 1974 and 2002, except for the year Marcia disappeared. He was also convicted of the 1975 murder of Vanderbilt University student Sarah Vannatta Des Prez.

Minister for Communications Malcolm Turnbull will be featured on the cover of GQ Australia's May issue, fueling speculation about his political ambitions. In an eight-page interview, Turnbull confirmed rumors that he had considered running for Prime Minister if Tony Abbott had been ousted in February's leadership spill. The interview covers Turnbull's childhood and political stance, and his previous appearance in GQ in 2013. Critics have accused Turnbull of fishing for votes with his high-profile magazine feature. However, Turnbull had previously stated that he was resigned to never again leading the Liberal Party and supporting Abbott's leadership.

A 14-year-old boy named Jack Cordero from Portland, Oregon, wrote a handwritten apology and included a Ben & Jerry's gift card for the staff at Powell's bookstore after vomiting in the store in March. The manager was impressed by the boy's good manners and the gesture made her day. The mess was described as "gigantic," and the apology letter went viral on social media, with many praising Jack's kindness and good nature.
